overall.assessment: Prema navedenoj strukturi, podcast snažno promiče evanđeoski ideal svetosti u svakodnevnom životu: Merz je prikazan kao laik koji vjeru povezuje s učenjem, radom, molitvom, liturgijom i služenjem mladima, a ne samo s privatnom pobožnošću. Taj spoj osobnog obraćenja, euharistije i apostolata odgovara crkvenom prikazu njegova života i može potaknuti slušatelje da kršćanski poziv žive u svojim konkretnim zanimanjima i društvenim odnosima. Teme javnog svjedočenja, mladih i međunarodnog širenja štovanja dodatno upućuju na misionarsku i zajedničarsku dimenziju vjere. Budući da je dostupna samo struktura, a ne cjelovit prijepis, nije moguće pouzdano prosuditi ton ni točnost pojedinih tvrdnji; zato je procjena usmjerena na tematski okvir.
seeds_of_logos: Predstavljanje svetosti laika u učiteljskoj i intelektualnoj svakodnevici pokazuje da kršćansko svjedočenje nije ograničeno na klerike ili samostanski život; crkveni prikaz Merza ističe ga kao vjernika laika, odgojitelja i uzor mladima.

Naglasak na euharistiji, molitvi i apostolatu daje duhovno središte njegovu djelovanju: u crkvenom tumačenju Merz je iz sudjelovanja u misi i hranjenja Kristovim tijelom i Božjom riječju crpio poticaj za apostolat mladih.

Teme javnog svjedočenja i izlaska iz „katakombi” mogu poticati odgovorno sudjelovanje vjernika u društvu, umjesto povlačenja vjere u privatnu sferu; crkveno predstavljanje Merza poziva mlade da budu misionari djelom i riječju te da zlo nadvladavaju snagom dobra.

Susret s mladima, filipinsko štovanje i svjedočanstva ljudi pružaju priliku da se svetost prikaže kao nadahnjujući poziv koji nadilazi nacionalne i generacijske granice, uz kulturu osobnog susreta i zajedništva.
Prikaz nastavničkog rada, odgoja i katoličkih organizacija može povezati vjeru s općim dobrom: crkveni nauk o svetosti laika izričito obuhvaća obrazovanje, komunikaciju, gospodarstvo, rad i politiku.
concerns: Struktura sadrži snažne elemente pobožnosti i pripovijesti o providnosti, grobu i čudu; u obradi je važno jasno razlikovati osobno svjedočanstvo i popularnu pobožnost od crkvene potvrde čuda ili kanonske prosudbe. Crkveni prikaz postupka beatifikacije pokazuje da štovanje i svjedočanstva pripadaju širem procesu, ali ne zamjenjuju crkveno razlučivanje.
overall.theological_context: Središnji teološki okvir jest krštenjem primljeni poziv svih vjernika na svetost i apostolat: crkveno tumačenje Merzova života povezuje svetost s liturgijom, Euharistijom, Božjom riječju i služenjem mladima, u skladu s naglascima koncilskih dokumenata Sacrosanctum Concilium i Apostolicam actuositatem. Socijalna dimenzija teme proizlazi iz poziva laicima da vjeru svjedoče u profesionalnom i javnom životu, služeći društvu i promičući dobro. Svetački primjer stoga nije samo predmet divljenja ili pobožnosti nego poticaj na osobni susret s Kristom, djelatnu ljubav i odgovorno sudjelovanje u zajednici.

overall.assessment_en: According to the stated structure, the podcast strongly promotes the evangelical ideal of holiness in everyday life: Merz is depicted as a layman who connects faith with study, work, prayer, liturgy, and service to young people, rather than only with private devotion. This combination of personal conversion, the Eucharist, and the apostolate corresponds to the Church's presentation of his life and can encourage listeners to live the Christian calling in their concrete occupations and social relationships. The themes of public witness, youth, and the international spread of veneration further point to the missionary and communitarian dimension of faith. Since only the structure is available, and not a complete transcript, it is not possible to reliably judge the tone or the accuracy of individual assertions; therefore, the assessment is focused on the thematic framework.
overall.theological_context_en: The central theological framework is the call received through baptism of all believers to holiness and the apostolate: the Church's interpretation of Merz's life connects holiness with liturgy, the Eucharist, the Word of God, and service to youth, in accordance with the emphases of the conciliar documents Sacrosanctum Concilium and Apostolicam actuositatem. The social dimension of the theme stems from the call to the laity to witness to the faith in professional and public life, serving society and promoting the good. The saintly example is therefore not merely an object of admiration or piety, but an encouragement to a personal encounter with Christ, active love, and responsible participation in the community.
seeds_of_logos_en: Presenting the holiness of the laity in teaching and intellectual everyday life shows that Christian witness is not limited to clerics or monastic life; the Church's depiction of Merz highlights him as a lay faithful, educator, and role model for young people.

The emphasis on the Eucharist, prayer, and the apostolate gives a spiritual center to his activity: in the Church's interpretation, Merz drew impetus for the apostolate of youth from participation in Mass and being nourished by Christ's Body and the Word of God.

The themes of public witness and emerging from the "catacombs" can encourage responsible participation of believers in society, instead of withdrawing faith into the private sphere; the Church's presentation of Merz calls young people to be missionaries in deed and word and to overcome evil with the power of good.

The encounter with young people, the Filipino veneration, and people's testimonies provide an opportunity to present holiness as an inspiring call that transcends national and generational boundaries, alongside a culture of personal encounter and communion.

The presentation of teaching work, education, and Catholic organizations can connect faith with the common good: Church teaching on the holiness of the laity explicitly encompasses education, communication, economy, labor, and politics.
concerns_en: The structure contains strong elements of piety and narratives about providence, the tomb, and a miracle; in addressing this, it is important to clearly distinguish personal testimony and popular piety from the Church's confirmation of a miracle or canonical judgment. The Church's account of the beatification process shows that veneration and testimonies belong to the broader process, but do not replace ecclesiastical discernment.

sections.subtitle: Od filipinske mladeži do zagrebačkog studija: razgovor o prvom laiku blaženiku Crkve u Hrvata
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pozdravlja gledatelje i predstavlja gosta, p. Božidara Nagyja, u studiju podcasta
sections.content:
Epizoda podcasta **ReDefinicija** otvara se isječkom koji odmah privlači pažnju. Gost, isusovac **p. Božidar Nagy**, govori o pravoj „eksploziji“ štovanja bl. Ivana Merza. Ta se eksplozija, kako ističe, najprije dogodila daleko od Hrvatske, na Filipinima, odmah nakon beatifikacije. Merza je tamo otkrila filipinska mladež. Posebno je za to zaslužan **Dave de la Cruz**, danas doktor, koji je tada imao tek osamnaest godina.

Voditelj zatim pozdravlja gledatelje tradicionalnim „Hvaljeni Isus i Marija i sveti Josip“ i predstavlja gosta. Ne skriva da jedva čeka otvoriti današnju temu, a to je blaženi Ivan Merz. P. Nagy zahvaljuje na pozivu i upućuje srdačan pozdrav slušateljima i gledateljima. Time počinje razgovor koji vodi od Merčeva djetinjstva u Banjoj Luci do dirljivih iskustava iz višedesetljetnog rada postulature.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: prikazuje širenje pobožnosti prema Ivanu Merzu i njegovu beatifikaciju bez tvrdnje koja bi proturječila vjeri ili Svetom pismu. Navod o naglom porastu štovanja na Filipinima i ulozi Davea de la Cruza povijesna je tvrdnja koju dostupni crkveni izvori ovdje ne potvrđuju, pa je ne treba smatrati provjerenom samo na temelju odlomka.
concerns: Izraz eksplozija štovanja može biti novinarski naglašen; sam po sebi nije teološki problem, ali ne potvrđuje opseg ni uzroke pobožnosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Beatifikacija dopušta da se Merza časti kao blaženika na mjestima i na način određenim crkvenim propisima; takvo štovanje nije isto što i klanjanje, koje pripada samo Bogu. Crkva predstavlja Merza kao uzor kršćanskog života: njegov rast u vjeri bio je povezan s liturgijom, euharistijom i apostolatom među mladima.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it depicts the spread of devotion toward Ivan Merz and his beatification without any claim that would contradict faith or Sacred Scripture. The statement about the sudden increase of veneration in the Philippines and the role of Dave de la Cruz is a historical claim that available church sources do not confirm here, so it should not be considered verified solely on the basis of the passage.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Beatification permits Merz to be venerated as a blessed in places and in the manner determined by church regulations; such veneration is not the same as adoration, which belongs to God alone. The Church presents Merz as a model of Christian life: his growth in faith was connected with the liturgy, the Eucharist, and the apostolate among the young.
concerns_en: The expression explosion of veneration may be journalistically emphasized; in itself it is not a theological problem, but it does not confirm the extent or the causes of the devotion.

sections.subtitle_en: From Filipino youth to a Zagreb studio: a conversation about the first lay blessed of the Church among the Croats
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host greets the viewers and introduces the guest, p. Božidar Nagy, in the podcast studio
sections.content_en:
The episode of the podcast **ReDefinicija** opens with a clip that immediately attracts attention. The guest, Jesuit **p. Božidar Nagy**, speaks about a true „explosion“ of veneration of Bl. Ivan Merz. That explosion, as he points out, first took place far from Croatia, in the Philippines, immediately after the beatification. Merz was discovered there by Filipino youth. Especially credited for this is **Dave de la Cruz**, today a doctor, who was then only eighteen years old.

The host then greets the viewers with the traditional „Praised be Jesus and Mary and Saint Joseph“ and introduces the guest. He does not hide that he can hardly wait to open today's topic, which is Blessed Ivan Merz. P. Nagy thanks for the invitation and sends a warm greeting to the listeners and viewers. With this begins the conversation that leads from Merz's childhood in Banja Luka to touching experiences from decades of work of the postulation.

sections.subtitle: Prvi vjernik laik na oltaru: titula koja Merza izdvaja
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy objašnjava da je Ivan Merz prvi vjernik laik blaženik u Crkvi u Hrvata
sections.content:
Na pitanje tko je bio blaženi Ivan Merz, p. Nagy kreće od njegove posljednje titule. Merz je **prvi vjernik laik u povijesti Crkve u Hrvata koji je uzdignut na oltar** kao blaženik i budući svetac.

Gost naglašava koliko je to značajno. Svi ostali hrvatski sveci i blaženici bili su svećenici, biskupi, časne sestre ili redovnici. Merz je, naprotiv, vjernik laik, i to suvremen, „moderan, iz naših dana“. Od njegove smrti uskoro će proći cijelo stoljeće, točnije za dvije godine. Ipak, kako p. Nagy kaže, „još uvijek je on tu“. Do nedavno su živjeli ljudi koji su ga osobno poznavali i s njim prijateljevali.

magisterium.assessment: Prikaz Merza kao blaženog vjernika laika i suvremenog uzora u osnovi je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: službena biografija potvrđuje njegovo proglašenje blaženim i laički stalež, a Crkva uči da su svi vjernici pozvani na svetost. Ipak, tvrdnje da je bio „prvi” u povijesti Crkve u Hrvata i da je „budući svetac” nisu potvrđene dostupnim izvorima; potonja formulacija može zvučati kao da je buduća kanonizacija zajamčena.
concerns: Dostupni izvori potvrđuju da je Ivan Merz laik i blaženik, ali ne potvrđuju prvenstvo među hrvatskim blaženicima niti tvrdnju da su svi ostali hrvatski sveci i blaženici bili članovi klera ili redovničkih zajednica.
Blaženstvo nije jamstvo buduće kanonizacije. Izraz „budući svetac” može se razumjeti kao nada ili očekivanje, ali ne bi ga trebalo iznositi kao već utvrđenu činjenicu.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk naglašava da poziv na svetost nije povlastica svećenika i redovnika: svi su krštenici, bez obzira na stalež, pozvani na puninu kršćanskoga života i savršenstvo ljubavi. Merzov primjer pokazuje kako se laički poziv na svetost može živjeti kroz svakodnevni život i apostolat, u njegovu slučaju osobito kroz liturgiju, euharistiju i služenje mladima. Blaženim je proglašen zbog vjernosti Kristu i svetosti života; sama je beatifikacija različita od kanonizacije.
magisterium.assessment_en: The presentation of Merz as a blessed lay faithful and a contemporary role model is fundamentally in accordance with Catholic teaching: the official biography confirms his beatification and lay state, and the Church teaches that all the faithful are called to holiness. Nevertheless, the claims that he was the „first” in the history of the Church among the Croats and that he is a „future saint” are not confirmed by available sources; the latter formulation may sound as if future canonization is guaranteed.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching emphasizes that the call to holiness is not a privilege of priests and religious: all the baptized, regardless of their state in life, are called to the fullness of Christian life and the perfection of charity. Merz's example shows how the lay call to holiness can be lived through daily life and the apostolate, in his case especially through the liturgy, the Eucharist, and service to young people. He was beatified because of his fidelity to Christ and holiness of life; beatification itself is distinct from canonization.
concerns_en: Available sources confirm that Ivan Merz is a layman and a blessed, but they do not confirm priority among Croatian blesseds, nor the claim that all other Croatian saints and blesseds were members of the clergy or religious communities.
Beatification is not a guarantee of future canonization. The expression „future saint” can be understood as a hope or expectation, but it should not be presented as an already established fact.

sections.subtitle_en: The first lay faithful on the altar: a title that sets Merz apart
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy explains that Ivan Merz is the first lay faithful blessed in the Church among the Croats
sections.content_en:
To the question of who Blessed Ivan Merz was, Fr. Nagy starts from his latest title. Merz is **the first lay faithful in the history of the Church among the Croats who was raised to the altar** as a blessed and a future saint.

The guest emphasizes how significant this is. All other Croatian saints and blesseds were priests, bishops, nuns, or religious. Merz, on the contrary, is a lay faithful, and a contemporary one, „modern, from our days“. A whole century will soon have passed since his death, more precisely in two years. Still, as Fr. Nagy says, „he is still here“. Until recently, people who knew him personally and were friends with him were living.

sections.subtitle: Austrougarska obitelj, željeznička stanica i čuvena banjalučka realka
sections.screenshot_description: Gost pripovijeda o Merčevu rođenju u Banjoj Luci 1896. i podrijetlu njegovih roditelja
sections.content:
Biografski se priča vraća na početak. Ivan Merz rođen je u **Banjoj Luci 1896. godine**, u obitelji koju p. Nagy opisuje kao tipično austrougarsku:

- **otac** je bio češki Nijemac iz Plzena u Češkoj,
- **majka** je bila iz Velike Kaniže u Mađarskoj.

Otac je završio vojnu akademiju i postao austrougarski časnik višeg ranga. Pretpostavljeni su ga poslali u Banju Luku, gdje je sve do preseljenja obitelji u Zagreb radio kao šef željezničke stanice.

Gost spominje i jedan mali detalj iz Merčeva školovanja. Prvi razred osnovne škole započeo je u Banjoj Luci, ali drugi i treći razred pohađao je u **Prijedoru**, jer je otac ondje bio premješten, također na željeznicu. Za četvrti razred obitelj se vratila u Banju Luku. Nakon osnovne škole Merz je upisao čuvenu **banjalučku realku**, gimnaziju u krasnoj zgradi koju je izgradila Austro-Ugarska.

Roditelji su ga dali u školu godinu dana ranije. Po Božjoj providnosti, kako primjećuje p. Nagy, to se kasnije pokazalo itekako važnim. Merz je tako **maturirao 1914. sa sedamnaest i pol godina, s odličnim uspjehom**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak iznosi biografske, a ne teološke tvrdnje, pa ne sadrži očito odstupanje od katoličkog nauka ili Svetoga pisma. Rođenje Ivana Merza u Banjoj Luci 1896. godine potvrđuje službena biografija, dok se ostali obiteljski i očev službeni detalji ne mogu provjeriti u dostupnim izvorima.
concerns: Podrijetlo roditelja, očev čin i vojna akademija te njegov rad kao šefa željezničke stanice nisu potvrđeni dostupnim izvorima; riječ je o biografskim pojedinostima, a ne o teološkom problemu.
magisterium.enrichment: Merzova biografija pokazuje kako se njegov životni put poslije povezao s katoličkim obrazovanjem i služenjem mladima: nakon školovanja posvetio se studiju i poučavanju, a postao je poznat kao apostol mladeži. Crkva ga predstavlja kao laika čiji su rad i svjedočanstvo bili ukorijenjeni u vjeri u Krista.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage makes biographical rather than theological claims, so it contains no apparent departure from Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. Ivan Merz's birth in Banja Luka in 1896 is confirmed by the official biography, while the other family details and father's service details cannot be verified in the available sources.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Merz's biography shows how his life path later became connected with Catholic education and ministry to young people: after his schooling, he dedicated himself to study and teaching, and became known as an apostle of youth. The Church presents him as a layman whose work and witness were rooted in faith in Christ.
concerns_en: The origin of the parents, the father's rank and military academy, and his work as head of the railway station are not confirmed by available sources; these are biographical details, not a theological issue.

sections.subtitle_en: An Austro-Hungarian family, a railway station, and the famous Banja Luka Realka
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest narrates about Merz's birth in Banja Luka in 1896 and the origins of his parents
sections.content_en:
Biographically, the story returns to the beginning. Ivan Merz was born in **Banja Luka in 1896**, in a family that Fr. Nagy describes as typically Austro-Hungarian:

- the **father** was a Czech German from Plzeň in Bohemia,
- the **mother** was from Nagykanizsa in Hungary.

The father completed the military academy and became a higher-ranking Austro-Hungarian officer. Superiors sent him to Banja Luka, where he worked as the head of the railway station until the family's relocation to Zagreb.

The guest also mentions one small detail from Merz's schooling. He started the first grade of elementary school in Banja Luka, but he attended the second and third grades in **Prijedor**, because his father was transferred there, also on the railway. For the fourth grade, the family returned to Banja Luka. After elementary school, Merz enrolled in the famous **Banja Luka Realka**, a gymnasium in a beautiful building built by Austria-Hungary.

His parents sent him to school a year earlier. By Divine Providence, as Fr. Nagy remarks, this later proved to be exceedingly important. Merz thus **graduated in 1914 at seventeen and a half years of age, with excellent success**.

sections.subtitle: „Katolik svjetovnjak spasio me za vječnost“: profesor Maraković i tajna ankete
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy govori o presudnom utjecaju profesora Ljubomira Marakovića na mladog Merza
sections.content:
Banjalučko razdoblje obilježio je snažan pozitivan utjecaj profesora **dr. Ljubomira Marakovića**. I on je bio izvanredan katolički laik. U Hrvatski katolički pokret uključio se još kao student književnosti u Beču, oko 1903. i 1904. godine. Na Merza je djelovao ne samo kulturno i književno nego i vjerski, pa mu je Maraković cijeli život ostao uzor.

P. Nagy zatim iznosi zanimljivu priču. Oko 1925. godine **dr. Kniewald**, kasnije Merčev veliki prijatelj, sastavljao je *Katolički đak*, molitvenik za katoličku mušku mladež. Za tu je priliku proveo veliku anonimnu anketu: intervjuirao je **400 mladića** i postavio im tridesetak pitanja. Zamolio je i Merza da ispuni upitnik. Od svih 400 odgovora jedino je Kniewald znao koji pripadaju Merzu. Odgovori su se sačuvali i danas čine svojevrsni **duhovni autoprofil** blaženika, objavljen u njegovim sabranim djelima.

Jedno je pitanje glasilo: kako su na mene, odnosno na moj vjerski život, djelovali profesori u srednjoj školi? Merz je odgovorio kratko: **„Katolik svjetovnjak spasio me za vječnost.“** Tada je imao 29 godina, tri godine prije smrti. Voditelj primjećuje da je riječ o retrogradnom pogledu. P. Nagy dodaje da su na Merza utjecale i mnoge druge osobe, ali ga je Maraković usmjerio na poseban način.

Maraković je Merza usmjerio i prema zvanju profesora književnosti. Sam se 1919. preselio u Zagreb, pokrenuo poznati časopis **Hrvatska prosvjeta** i bio vrlo cijenjen kao književni kritičar. Trebao je postati i sveučilišni profesor, ali su tada nastupili neki problemi. To je, kako gost kaže, „druga tema“.

magisterium.assessment: Opis je u skladu s katoličkim naukom jer prikazuje kako laik može svjedočanstvom vjere, kulturnim radom i osobnim primjerom utjecati na duhovni život drugih. Izraz „spasio me za vječnost” najbolje je razumjeti kao slikovit opis Marakovićeva posrednog utjecaja, a ne kao tvrdnju da čovjek samostalno daje spasenje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk uči da su i laici pozvani na svetost te da svoj poziv žive i svjedoče u svakodnevnom životu i društvenim okolnostima. Njihov primjer može druge privesti Kristu, ali izvor spasenja ostaje Bog; laičko svjedočenje djeluje kao sredstvo evangelizacije i poticaj na vjeru.
magisterium.assessment_en: The description is in accordance with Catholic teaching because it shows how a layman, through the witness of faith, cultural work, and personal example, can influence the spiritual life of others. The expression "saved me for eternity" is best understood as a figurative description of Maraković's indirect influence, and not as an assertion that man independently grants salvation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching teaches that the laity are also called to holiness and that they live out and witness to their vocation in everyday life and social circumstances. Their example can lead others to Christ, but the source of salvation remains God; lay witness acts as an instrument of evangelization and an encouragement to faith.

sections.subtitle_en: "A lay Catholic saved me for eternity": Professor Maraković and the secret of the survey
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Nagy speaks about the decisive influence of Professor Ljubomir Maraković on the young Merz
sections.content_en:
The Banja Luka period was marked by the strong positive influence of Professor **Dr. Ljubomir Maraković**. He too was an outstanding Catholic layman. He joined Hrvatski katolički pokret while still a literature student in Beč, around the years 1903 and 1904. He influenced Merz not only culturally and literarily, but also religiously, so Maraković remained his role model for his entire life.

Fr. Nagy then presents an interesting story. Around 1925, **Dr. Kniewald**, later a great friend of Merz, was compiling *Katolički đak*, a prayer book for Catholic male youth. For that occasion, he conducted a large anonymous survey: he interviewed **400 young men** and asked them about thirty questions. He also asked Merz to fill out the questionnaire. Of all 400 answers, only Kniewald knew which ones belonged to Merz. The answers have been preserved and today constitute a kind of **spiritual self-profile** of the blessed, published in his collected works.

One question read: how did high school teachers affect me, that is, my religious life? Merz answered briefly: **"A lay Catholic saved me for eternity."** He was 29 years old at the time, three years before his death. The host notes that this is a retrospective view. Fr. Nagy adds that many other persons also influenced Merz, but Maraković directed him in a special way.

Maraković also guided Merz toward the profession of literature professor. He himself moved to Zagreb in 1919, launched the well-known journal **Hrvatska prosvjeta**, and was highly esteemed as a literary critic. He was also supposed to become a university professor, but then some problems arose. That is, as the guest says, "another topic".

sections.subtitle: Od vojne akademije do Dolomita: rat koji je razbio „estetski katolicizam“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost opisuje Merčev odlazak u vojnu akademiju i kasnije na talijansko bojište
sections.content:
Nakon mature Merz je, na želju roditelja koji su htjeli da postane časnik poput oca, upisao **vojnu akademiju u Bečkom Novom Mjestu**. Za vojništvo, međutim, nije imao nikakve volje. Nakon tri mjeseca, pred Božić 1914., napustio je akademiju. Već u siječnju upisao je fakultet u Beču.

Studij je trajao svega godinu dana jer je bjesnio **Prvi svjetski rat**. Merz je pozvan na vojnu obuku u veljači 1916., najprije u Grazu, a zatim na tečajeve na kojima je osposobljen za skijaškog vođu postrojbi u sjevernoj Italiji, u Dolomitima. Krajem 1916. poslan je na **talijansko bojište**, gdje je proveo dvije godine, sve do kraja rata.

P. Nagy ističe da je upravo ratno razdoblje na Merza najviše djelovalo u vjerskom smislu. U jednom članku Merz je sam zapisao da je do rata njegov katolicizam bio **„estetski katolicizam“**, a da je nakon rata spoznao pravi kršćanski život koji treba voditi. Život mu je bio vrlo često ugrožen, od bombi i svih drugih opasnosti, ali ga je, kako gost kaže, dragi Bog sačuvao.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ne iznosi tvrdnju koja bi proturječila katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu, a glavni životni slijed — kratko pohađanje vojne akademije, studij u Beču i odlazak u vojsku tijekom Prvoga svjetskog rata — uglavnom se podudara sa službenom biografijom Ivana Merza. Ipak, pojedinosti o točnom razlogu napuštanja akademije, siječanjskom upisu, obuci u Grazu i skijaškom tečaju nisu sve potvrđene navedenim crkvenim izvorima.
concerns: Službena biografija navodi da je Merz napustio vojnu akademiju nakon kratkog razdoblja zbog zgražanja nad ondje raširenim pokvarenim običajima, a ne samo zbog manjka volje za vojništvom; bilježi upis na Bečko sveučilište 1915. i novačenje u ožujku 1916.
Dostupni crkveni izvori ne potvrđuju pojedinosti o obuci u Grazu i skijaškom osposobljavanju.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni prikaz Merzova života ističe da ga je ratno iskustvo, usred svjedočenja ratnim strahotama, potaknulo na dublje predanje Bogu i odlučnost da teži kršćanskom savršenstvu. To je u skladu s kršćanskim razumijevanjem da patnja nije sama po sebi dobro, ali se može, uz Božju pomoć, pretvoriti u povod za obraćenje i vjernost; Merzov dnevnički zapis iz 1918. izražava želju da ne zaboravi Boga i da se sjedini s njim.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage makes no claim that would contradict Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture, and the main life sequence — brief attendance at the military academy, studies in Beč, and departure for the army during the First World War — broadly coincides with the official biography of Ivan Merz. Nevertheless, the details regarding the exact reason for leaving the academy, the January enrollment, the training in Graz, and the ski course are not all confirmed by the cited church sources.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church's account of Merz's life emphasizes that the war experience, amidst witnessing the horrors of war, prompted him toward a deeper surrender to God and a determination to strive for Christian perfection. This is in accordance with the Christian understanding that suffering is not a good in itself, but can, with God's help, be turned into an occasion for conversion and fidelity; Merz's diary entry from 1918 expresses the desire not to forget God and to be united with him.
concerns_en: The official biography states that Merz left the military academy after a short period due to horror at the corrupt customs widespread there, and not merely due to a lack of will for soldiering; it records enrollment at the University of Beč in 1915 and conscription in March 1916.
Available church sources do not confirm the details regarding training in Graz and ski instruction.

sections.subtitle_en: From the military academy to the Dolomites: the war that shattered "aesthetic Catholicism"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest describes Merz's departure to the military academy and later to the Italian front
sections.content_en:
After high school graduation, at the wish of his parents who wanted him to become an officer like his father, Merz enrolled in the **military academy in Bečko Novo Mjesto**. For soldiering, however, he had no inclination whatsoever. After three months, before Christmas 1914, he left the academy. Already in January, he enrolled in university in Beč.

His studies lasted only one year because the **First World War** was raging. Merz was called up for military training in February 1916, first in Graz, and then for courses where he was trained as a ski leader of units in northern Italy, in the Dolomites. At the end of 1916, he was sent to the **Italian front**, where he spent two years, until the end of the war.

Fr. Nagy emphasizes that it was precisely the war period that affected Merz the most in a religious sense. In an article, Merz himself wrote that before the war his Catholicism was **"aesthetic Catholicism"**, and that after the war he realized the true Christian life that ought to be led. His life was very often in danger, from bombs and all other hazards, but, as the guest says, the dear God preserved him.

sections.subtitle: Beč, Pariz, Zagreb: „Umro je kao svetac jer je živio kao svetac“
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy govori o Merčevu studiju u Parizu i citira francuski dnevnik La Croix
sections.content:
Krajem rata 1918. Merz se u jesen vratio u Banju Luku. Već u siječnju otišao je u Beč i nastavio studij. Ondje je proveo dvije godine, 1919. i 1920. U jesen 1920. dobio je **stipendiju za Pariz** od jedne katoličke udruge. To je isposlovao isusovac **p. Miroslav Vanin**. Stipendije su dobili Merz i još dvojica dobrih katoličkih mladića. Ključnu ulogu ponovno je odigrao Maraković, koji je Merza predložio među tom trojicom.

U Parizu je Merz proveo dvije godine i skupljao materijal za doktorsku disertaciju. Nakon povratka 1922. dovršio ju je i obranio na **Zagrebačkom sveučilištu**. U Zagrebu je zatim proveo šest godina, sve do svoje svetačke smrti, i ostavio trag „kakav si čovjek može samo zamisliti jedan svetac“.

P. Nagy prenosi i ocjenu Francuza koji su ga dobro upoznali. U katoličkom dnevniku **La Croix** (Križ) napisali su: **„Ivan Merz je umro kao svetac jer je živio kao svetac.“** Voditelj to sažima riječima: „Kratko i jasno.“

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: opis Merzova studija i njegova puta prema doktoratu podudara se s crkvenom biografijom, a predstavljanje njegova života kao svetačkog primjera odgovara njegovu proglašenju blaženim zbog herojskog življenja kršćanskih kreposti. Izraz „umro je kao svetac jer je živio kao svetac” prikladan je kao sažetak, pod uvjetom da ne sugerira da se svetost zaslužuje neovisno o Božjoj milosti.
concerns: Dostupni crkveni životopis potvrđuje Merzov boravak u Beču i Parizu te doktorat iz filozofije, ali ne potvrđuje pojedinosti o stipendiji ni o tome tko ju je isposlovao; te bi biografske tvrdnje trebalo provjeriti zasebno.
Merz je službeno blaženik, a ne kanonizirani svetac; izraz „živio kao svetac” može se razumjeti u općem smislu svetoga života, ali ne treba ga zamijeniti za formalnu kanonizaciju.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkvena biografija navodi da je Merz nakon rata nastavio studij u Beču, a zatim u Parizu pripremio disertaciju kojom je stekao doktorat iz filozofije na Zagrebačkom sveučilištu. Njegova svetost nije predstavljena samo kao rezultat ljudske discipline: u njegovu životu ističu se težnja za sjedinjenjem s Bogom, vjernost kršćanskom pozivu i herojsko vršenje kreposti, koje je Crkva priznala u postupku beatifikacije. Kršćanski primjer svetih zato upućuje na Božje djelovanje i potiče vjernike da nasljeduju Krista u vlastitom životnom staležu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: the description of Merz's studies and his path toward a doctorate corresponds with the ecclesial biography, and presenting his life as a saintly example corresponds with his beatification for heroic practice of Christian virtues. The expression "he died like a saint because he lived like a saint" is fitting as a summary, provided it does not suggest that holiness is earned independently of God's grace.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The ecclesial biography states that after the war Merz continued his studies in Vienna, and then in Paris prepared the dissertation by which he earned a doctorate in philosophy at the University of Zagreb. His holiness is not presented merely as the result of human discipline: his life highlights the striving for union with God, fidelity to the Christian vocation, and heroic practice of virtues, which the Church recognized in the process of beatification. The Christian example of the saints therefore points to God's action and encourages the faithful to imitate Christ in their own state of life.
concerns_en: The available ecclesial biography confirms Merz's stay in Vienna and Paris and the doctorate in philosophy, but does not confirm details about the scholarship or about who arranged it; these biographical claims should be verified separately.
Merz is officially a blessed, not a canonized saint; the expression "lived like a saint" can be understood in the general sense of a holy life, but it should not be mistaken for formal canonization.

sections.subtitle_en: Vienna, Paris, Zagreb: "He died like a saint because he lived like a saint"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Nagy speaks about Merz's studies in Paris and quotes the French daily La Croix
sections.content_en:
At the end of the war in 1918, in the autumn, Merz returned to Banja Luka. Already in January he went to Vienna and continued his studies. He spent two years there, 1919 and 1920. In the autumn of 1920, he received a **scholarship for Paris** from a Catholic association. This was arranged by the Jesuit **Fr. Miroslav Vanin**. Merz and two other good Catholic young men received scholarships. Maraković once again played a key role, proposing Merz among those three.

In Paris, Merz spent two years and gathered material for his doctoral dissertation. After returning in 1922, he completed it and defended it at the **University of Zagreb**. He then spent six years in Zagreb, until his saintly death, and left an impact "such as man can only imagine a saint would leave".

Fr. Nagy also conveys the assessment of the French who got to know him well. In the Catholic daily **La Croix** (Cross) they wrote: **"Ivan Merz died like a saint because he lived like a saint."** The host summarizes this with the words: "Short and clear."

sections.subtitle: Ratni dnevnik i program od 5. veljače 1918.: „Boga nikad ne zaboraviti“
sections.screenshot_description: Gost citira Merčeve prve životne odluke zapisane u ratnom dnevniku 5. veljače 1918.
sections.content:
Voditelj primjećuje da je Merz u kratkom vremenu proživio mnogo, što se vidi i u njegovu dnevniku i radovima. Pita gosta koje mu je razdoblje Merčeva života najzanimljivije. P. Nagy bez dvojbe izdvaja **ratni period**. U njemu je Merz vodio dnevnik u kojem se vide njegova razmišljanja o prolaznosti života i smrti. Smrti je gledao u oči gotovo svaki dan, kao i brojnim poginulima. Upravo su ti trenuci, kako gost kaže, pročišćavali njegov pogled, pa je na život počeo gledati „sasvim drugim očima“.

Potkraj rata Merz je ocu napisao: **„Zahvalan sam Bogu što sam sudjelovao u ratu jer sam u ratu spoznao tolike stvari koje inače nikad ne bih spoznao.“** Dodao je da jedva čeka vratiti se kući i uskladiti život s pravim kršćanskim smislom, „i tako je i bilo“.

P. Nagy posebno ističe jedan datum koji gledatelji mogu sami provjeriti u ratnom dnevniku: **5. veljače 1918.** Toga je dana Merz zapisao svoj prvi životni program, odnosno odluke kako će živjeti nakon rata. Program počinje rečenicom: **„Boga nikad, nikad ne zaboraviti. Uvijek težiti za sjedinjenjem s Njime.“** Slijede odluke o postu, asketskom životu i molitvi. Gost taj tekst preporučuje svima.

Merz je svoje odluke cijeli život usavršavao i nadopunjavao. Svake je godine obavljao duhovne vježbe i na njima donosio nove odluke. One sa zadnjih duhovnih vježbi napisao je na pisaćem stroju i stavio u **misal** iz kojega je svakodnevno pratio misu. S tim je misalom otišao i na operaciju u bolnicu, tako da su ga odluke pratile praktički do smrti. Voditelj zaključuje da ga je rat formirao i da se ta formacija dalje prenosi.

magisterium.assessment: Opis Merčeva ratnog iskustva kao poticaja na ozbiljnije promišljanje o prolaznosti i smrti te na pročišćenje pogleda na život u skladu je s katoličkim naukom. Službena biografija potvrđuje da ga je ratno iskustvo duhovno sazrijevalo i potaknulo da, oslanjajući se na Boga, teži kršćanskom savršenstvu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička tradicija ne smatra smrt konačnom riječju o ljudskom životu: sjećanje na smrtnost može potaknuti čovjeka da ozbiljnije traži Boga i ispuni svoj život dobrim. Kršćanska nada pritom ne uljepšava rat ni patnju, nego nalazi smisao u vjernom odgovoru na njih i u pouzdanju da Kristova uskrsna pobjeda nadilazi smrt.

citations.document_author: Dicastery for the Causes of Saints

citations.document_title: 3 November 2008: Mass in suffrage for Cardinals and Bishops who have died in the past year

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of Merz's war experience as an incentive for more serious reflection on transience and death, as well as for the purification of his outlook on life, is in accordance with Catholic teaching. The official biography confirms that the war experience matured him spiritually and prompted him, relying on God, to strive for Christian perfection.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic tradition does not consider death to be the final word on human life: the remembrance of mortality can encourage a person to seek God more seriously and fulfill their life with good. In doing so, Christian hope does not embellish war or suffering, but finds meaning in a faithful response to them and in the trust that Christ's Easter victory transcends death.

sections.subtitle_en: War Diary and Program of February 5, 1918: "Never to Forget God"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest quotes Merz's first life resolutions recorded in the war diary on February 5, 1918.
sections.content_en:
The host observes that Merz experienced a great deal in a short time, which is evident in both his diary and his works. He asks the guest which period of Merz's life is most interesting to him. Fr. Nagy without hesitation singles out the **war period**. In it, Merz kept a diary in which his reflections on the transience of life and death are visible. He looked death in the eyes almost every day, as well as numerous deceased. It was precisely those moments, as the guest says, that purified his outlook, so that he began to look at life "with completely different eyes".

Toward the end of the war, Merz wrote to his father: **"I am grateful to God that I participated in the war because in the war I learned so many things that I otherwise never would have learned."** He added that he could hardly wait to return home and align his life with the true Christian meaning, "and so it was".

Fr. Nagy especially highlights one date that viewers can check for themselves in the war diary: **February 5, 1918**. On that day, Merz wrote down his first life program, that is, resolutions on how he would live after the war. The program begins with the sentence: **"Never, never forget God. Always strive for union with Him."** Resolutions on fasting, ascetic life, and prayer follow. The guest recommends this text to everyone.

Merz perfected and supplemented his resolutions throughout his entire life. Every year he made spiritual exercises and made new resolutions during them. The ones from his last spiritual exercises he typed on a typewriter and placed into the **missal** from which he followed Mass daily. With that missal he also went to the hospital for surgery, so that the resolutions accompanied him practically until death. The host concludes that the war formed him and that this formation continues to be passed on.

sections.subtitle: Svetost za katedrom: profesor francuskog i njemačkog kao uzor laicima
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy objašnjava kako je Merz ostvario svetost u svjetovnom zanimanju
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim postavlja pitanje koje često čuje: nisu li svi sveci isti? Po čemu je onda Ivan Merz specifičan?

P. Nagy odgovara da je Merz prije svega **prvi laik u Crkvi u Hrvata kojemu je službeno priznata svetost života**. Ima, dodaje, još mnogo vjernika laika koje bi bilo vrijedno uzdići na oltar, ali to je dug proces. Kod Merza je prepoznato da je kreposti živio u herojskom stupnju.

Merz je pokazao da je moguće **živjeti kao svjetovnjak u svijetu, imati svjetovno zanimanje i postati svetac**. Nakon studija književnosti bio je profesor **francuskog i njemačkog jezika na Nadbiskupskoj gimnaziji**. Gost naglašava da je bez obzira na to što je škola bila nadbiskupijska predavao običan, svjetovni predmet. Nije predavao vjeronauk. Upravo je vršeći to svakodnevno zanimanje ostvarivao svetost života.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je u skladu s katoličkim naukom da su laici pozvani na svetost upravo kroz svakodnevne i profesionalne obveze, a Merzov je život Crkva prepoznala kao primjer kršćanskoga laičkog svjedočenja. Tvrdnju da je bio prvi laik u Crkvi u Hrvata kojemu je službeno priznata svetost nije moguće potvrditi dostupnim izvorima, pa je treba izreći uz povijesnu provjeru.
concerns: Dostupni izvori potvrđuju da je Merz bio laik, da je proglašen blaženim i da su njegove kreposti proglašene herojskima, ali ne potvrđuju tvrdnju da je bio prvi takav laik u Crkvi u Hrvata.
Precizno je govoriti o blaženom Ivanu Merzu, a ne o kanoniziranom svecu: beatifikacija i priznanje herojskih kreposti ne znače da je osoba kanonizirana.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva naučava da svjetovne i profesionalne obveze laika nisu zapreka svetosti, nego mogu biti mjesto služenja Bogu i bližnjima; to povezuje s Pavlovim pozivom da se sve čini u ime Gospodina (Kol 3,17). Merz je bio profesor francuskoga jezika, a Sveta Stolica je njegove teološke i stožerne kreposti proglasila herojskima; njegov primjer zato svjedoči o svetosti koja se živi u svakodnevnom radu, a ne samo izvan svjetovnih zanimanja.

citations.document_author: Dicastery for the Causes of Saints

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is in accordance with Catholic teaching that the laity are called to holiness precisely through everyday and professional obligations, and the Church recognized Merz's life as an example of Christian lay witness. The claim that he was the first layperson in the Church among Croats whose holiness was officially recognized cannot be confirmed by available sources, so it should be stated with historical verification.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church teaches that the secular and professional obligations of the laity are not an obstacle to holiness, but can be a place of service to God and neighbor; this connects with Paul's call to do everything in the name of the Lord (Col 3:17). Merz was a professor of the French language, and the Holy See declared his theological and cardinal virtues heroic; his example therefore bears witness to holiness lived in everyday work, and not only outside secular professions.
concerns_en: Available sources confirm that Merz was a layperson, that he was beatified, and that his virtues were declared heroic, but they do not confirm the claim that he was the first such layperson in the Church among Croats.
It is precise to speak of Blessed Ivan Merz, rather than a canonized saint: beatification and recognition of heroic virtues do not mean that a person is canonized.

sections.subtitle_en: Holiness at the lectern: a professor of French and German as a role model for laypeople
sections.screenshot_description_en: P. Nagy explains how Merz achieved holiness in a secular profession
sections.content_en:
The host then asks a question he often hears: are not all saints the same? What makes Ivan Merz specific, then?

P. Nagy replies that Merz is, above all, **the first layperson in the Church among Croats whose holiness of life has been officially recognized**. There are, he adds, still many lay faithful who would be worthy of being raised to the altar, but that is a long process. With Merz, it was recognized that he lived the virtues to a heroic degree.

Merz showed that it is possible **to live as a layperson in the world, have a secular profession, and become a saint**. After studying literature, he was a professor of **French and German at the Nadbiskupska gimnazija**. The guest emphasizes that, regardless of the fact that the school was archdiocesan, he taught an ordinary, secular subject. He did not teach religious education. It was precisely by performing that everyday occupation that he attained holiness of life.

sections.subtitle: Pet poruka jedne slike: kravata, knjiga, tornjevi, golub i euharistija
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy pokazuje sliku bl. Ivana Merza autora Ante Mamuše koja visi iza sugovornika
sections.content:
P. Nagy upozorava gledatelje na sliku iza sugovornika. Naslikao ju je **Anto Mamuša**, akademski slikar iz Novog Travnika u Bosni, poznat po brojnim religioznim motivima. Prema gostovim riječima, slikar je na njoj savršeno prikazao profil blaženika. Iz slike se može iščitati **pet poruka**:

- **Laik u civilu.** Mladi čovjek s kravatom pod vratom živio je u svijetu, imao svjetovno zanimanje i ostvario svetost.
- **Knjiga.** Simbol učenosti, kulture i znanosti. Merz je povezao vjeru, znanost i kulturu i pokazao da one ne samo mogu nego i *trebaju* ići zajedno. Doktorat pod naslovom *Utjecaj liturgije na francuske književnike* objavljen je u Parizu nakon beatifikacije. Francuzi su ocijenili da je Merz obradio temu koju dotad nitko od njih nije obradio, pa ga književni krugovi ondje vrlo cijene. Njegov duhovnik **p. Vrbanek** svjedočio je da je Merz poznavao deset jezika: pet je lijepo govorio, a na pet je imao pasivno znanje. Voditelj ga naziva „pravim eruditom“.
- **Tornjevi crkava.** Na slici su banjalučka katedrala, zagrebačka katedrala i Bazilika sv. Petra. Oni izražavaju Merčevu duboku crkvenost. Njegov prijatelj **Dušan Žanko** rekao je da u liku Ivana Merza nema jače ideje od ideje Crkve, koja kroz liturgiju daje hvalu Bogu, a preko hijerarhije i papinstva čuva jedinstvo.
- **Bijeli golub, simbol Duha Svetoga.** Duh Sveti nadahnjivao je i vodio Merza te od njega učinio velikog apostola i svjedoka vjere, kao što je nekoć promijenio apostole.
- **Euharistija.** Prikazana je pokraj njegove glave jer je bila sastavni dio njegove duhovnosti. Već kao student svakodnevno je išao na misu i pričest, osobito u Zagrebu. To je nedavno u propovijedi na blagdan blaženika u Zagrebu posebno istaknuo i banjalučki biskup **Franjo Komarica**.

To su, zaključuje p. Nagy, poruke kojima Merz svjedoči i koje vjernici mogu nasljedovati.

magisterium.assessment: Prikaz Ivana Merza kao laika koji je živio u svijetu i težio svetosti dobro je usklađen s katoličkim naukom: Crkva uči da su i laici pozvani na svetost u svakodnevnim životnim okolnostima, a Merz je upravo takav primjer. Povezivanje knjige s učenjem i kulture s vjerom razumna je simbolička interpretacija, premda sama po sebi nije nauk Crkve niti tvrdnja koju je moguće procijeniti kao obvezujuću doktrinarnu činjenicu.
concerns: Izraz da slika „savršeno” prikazuje blaženikov profil predstavlja estetski sud, a tumačenje elemenata slike osobnu ili umjetničku simboliku, ne službeno crkveno tumačenje.
Dostavljeni odlomak završava nedovršenom rečenicom pa se ostale najavljene poruke slike ne mogu procijeniti.
magisterium.enrichment: Svetost laika ne znači napuštanje svijeta, nego življenje kršćanskog poziva u poslu, učenju i društvenom životu, oslonjeno na sjedinjenost s Kristom. U propovijedi beatifikacije Ivana Merza sveti Ivan Pavao II. ističe da su ga liturgija, misa, Kristovo tijelo i Božja riječ oblikovali za apostolat mladih; zato knjiga u prikazu može prikladno upućivati na obrazovanje koje nije odvojeno od vjere.

sections.subtitle_en: Five messages of one painting: tie, book, towers, dove, and Eucharist
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Nagy points to the painting of Bl. Ivan Merz by Anto Mamuša hanging behind the interlocutor
sections.content_en:
Fr. Nagy draws the viewers' attention to the painting behind the interlocutor. It was painted by **Anto Mamuša**, an academic painter from Novi Travnik in Bosnia, known for numerous religious motifs. According to the guest's words, the painter perfectly depicted the profile of the beatus in it. **Five messages** can be read from the painting:

- **A layman in civilian clothes.** A young man with a tie around his neck lived in the world, had a secular profession, and attained holiness.
- **A book.** A symbol of erudition, culture, and science. Merz connected faith, science, and culture and showed that they not only can but *must* go together. His doctorate titled *The Influence of the Liturgy on French Writers* was published in Paris after the beatification. The French assessed that Merz covered a topic that none of them had covered until then, so literary circles there hold him in high regard. His spiritual director **Fr. Vrbanek** testified that Merz knew ten languages: he spoke five well, and in five he had a passive knowledge. The host calls him a “true polymath”.
- **Church towers.** The painting features the Banja Luka Cathedral, the Zagreb Cathedral, and St. Peter's Basilica. They express Merz's deep ecclesiality. His friend **Dušan Žanko** said that in the figure of Ivan Merz there is no stronger idea than the idea of the Church, which gives praise to God through the liturgy, and preserves unity through the hierarchy and the papacy.
- **A white dove, symbol of the Holy Spirit.** The Holy Spirit inspired and guided Merz and made him a great apostle and witness of faith, just as He once transformed the apostles.
- **The Eucharist.** It is depicted next to his head because it was an integral part of his spirituality. Already as a student, he went to Mass and Holy Communion daily, especially in Zagreb. The Bishop of Banja Luka, **Franjo Komarica**, also particularly emphasized this recently in his homily on the feast day of the beatus in Zagreb.

These are, Fr. Nagy concludes, the messages that Merz bears witness to and that the faithful can imitate.

sections.subtitle: Zaboravljeni blaženik u novom zamahu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj uspoređuje porast štovanja bl. Ivana Merza s 'eksplozijom' štovanja sv. Josipa
sections.content:
Voditelj iznosi svoj dojam. Iako je Merz 2003. u Banjoj Luci uzdignut na oltar, njegovo je štovanje posljednjih desetljeća bilo prilično zanemareno. Tek sada, smatra, dolazi do prave „eksplozije“ štovanja i nove valorizacije njegova lika i djela.

Kao primjer navodi da u Zagrebu postoje praktički dvije zajednice koje Merza štuju i formiraju se na njegovu primjeru. Među njima je i bratstvo **Vitezovi Bezgrešnog Srca Marijina**, koje prolazi formaciju po blaženom Ivanu Merzu. Voditelj napominje da sam Merz to nije tako nazivao jer je riječ o današnjem terminu. Povlači i usporedbu sa **sv. Josipom**, koji je stoljećima bio skriven, a danas doživljava pravi procvat štovanja. Pita gosta što je uzrok tome.

P. Nagy odgovara: „Konačno, Bogu hvala da je došlo do toga.“ Dodaje, međutim, da se prva eksplozija dogodila dvadeset godina ranije, na Filipinima, odmah nakon beatifikacije.

magisterium.assessment: Opis štovanja blaženoga Ivana Merza i oblikovanja zajednice prema njegovu primjeru uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: Crkva ističe blaženike kao svjedoke i uzore kršćanskoga života. Tvrdnje o tome koliko je štovanje bilo zanemareno i je li sada nastupila „eksplozija” predstavljene su kao voditeljev dojam, pa ih ovaj odlomak ne potvrđuje kao provjerene činjenice.
concerns: Izraz „štovanje” treba razumjeti kao crkveno iskazivanje počasti blaženiku, a ne kao klanjanje koje pripada samo Bogu; odlomak ne pokazuje da voditelj te pojmove miješa.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva uči da primjeri svetih i blaženih potiču vjernike da ustraju na putu prema svetosti, što je povezano s biblijskom slikom „oblaka svjedoka” (Heb 12,1). Svrha štovanja nije samo umnažanje vanjskih pobožnih čina, nego proslava Boga i produbljivanje ljubavi koja se očituje u kršćanskom životu; nasljedovanje Merza stoga je najplodnije kada vodi Kristu i djelatnoj ljubavi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the veneration of Blessed Ivan Merz and the shaping of the community according to his example is largely in accordance with Catholic teaching: the Church highlights the blessed as witnesses and role models of Christian life. The claims regarding how much the devotion was neglected and whether an "explosion" has now occurred are presented as the host's impression, so this passage does not confirm them as verified facts.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church teaches that the examples of the saints and blessed encourage the faithful to persevere on the path toward holiness, which is connected to the biblical image of the "cloud of witnesses" (Heb 12:1). The purpose of veneration is not merely multiplying external acts of piety, but the glorification of God and the deepening of charity manifested in Christian life; imitating Merz is therefore most fruitful when it leads to Christ and active charity.
concerns_en: The term "veneration" should be understood as the ecclesial rendering of honor to a blessed, and not as Eucharistic adoration (adoratio) which belongs only to God; the passage does not show that the host confuses these concepts.

sections.subtitle_en: A Forgotten Blessed in a New Momentum
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host compares the rise in devotion to Bl. Ivan Merz to an 'explosion' of devotion to Saint Joseph
sections.content_en:
The host expresses his impression. Although Merz was raised to the altars in Banja Luka in 2003, devotion to him in recent decades was quite neglected. Only now, he believes, is there a true "explosion" of devotion and a new valorization of his figure and work.

As an example, he cites that in Zagreb there are practically two communities that venerate Merz and are formed according to his example. Among them is the brotherhood **Vitezovi Bezgrešnog Srca Marijina**, which undergoes formation according to Blessed Ivan Merz. The host notes that Merz himself did not call it that because it is a contemporary term. He also draws a comparison with **Saint Joseph**, who was hidden for centuries, and today is experiencing a true flourishing of devotion. He asks the guest what the cause of this is.

Fr. Nagy replies: "Finally, thank God that it has come to that." He adds, however, that the first explosion occurred twenty years earlier, in the Philippines, immediately after the beatification.

sections.subtitle: Domaća zadaća koja je promijenila život: kako je Dave de la Cruz „proguglao“ Merza
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy prepričava kako je mladi Filipinac na internetu otkrio bl. Ivana Merza
sections.content:
P. Nagy naglašava da nitko iz Hrvatske nije išao širiti Merčevo štovanje na Filipine. Priču mu je ispričao sam **Dave de la Cruz**, tada osamnaestogodišnjak. Bio je dobar ministrant, usko povezan s Crkvom, pa ga je župnik poslao na liturgijski tečaj u njegovu gradu.

Profesor je polaznicima zadao domaću zadaću: pronaći na internetu svece posebno povezane s liturgijom. Poslušni student u tražilicu je upisao „sveci liturgija“. Kako je kasnije ispričao, **prvo ime koje se pojavilo na ekranu bilo je Ivan Merz**. Za njega nikad nije čuo.

Postulatura je tada već imala web stranicu i dosta tekstova prevedenih na engleski. Mladić je sve pročitao i oduševio se, „nešto ga je zapalilo“. Odmah se javio postulaturi i tražio što više podataka. Poslali su mu slike, sličice i relikvije druge klase. Uz pomoć roditelja, koji su bili boljeg imovinskog stanja, **2007. doputovao je avionom u Zagreb na Merčev grob**.

U Zagrebu je dobio dodatne informacije i literaturu. Po povratku je osnovao **udrugu mladih** koja štuje svece, a na poseban način bl. Ivana Merza. Udruga danas broji oko **200 članova** i ima vlastiti centar, kuću. P. Nagy primjećuje da takvo nešto „mi još nemamo ovdje“. U kući je kapelica bl. Ivana Merza s relikvijama i slikama, „upravo nešto nevjerojatno“. Sve se to može vidjeti na njihovoj web stranici.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: prikazuje liturgijsko obrazovanje i zanimanje za bl. Ivana Merza kao poticaj na upoznavanje njegova kršćanskog svjedočanstva, bez iznošenja tvrdnje protivne vjeri. Prema dostupnom tekstu, riječ je o osobnoj anegdoti, a ne o tvrdnji da je rezultat internetske tražilice dokaz Božje objave ili čudo.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva je službeno istaknula Merzov rast u kršćanskoj zrelosti kroz liturgiju te povezanost njegova sudjelovanja u misi, hranjenja Kristovim Tijelom i Riječju Božjom s apostolatom među mladima. Štovanje blaženih u katoličkom smislu usmjereno je na zahvalno spominjanje njihova primjera i nasljedovanje kršćanskog života; zato je korisno ovu priču razumjeti kao početak zanimanja za Merzovo svjedočanstvo, a ne kao potvrdu da internetski algoritam ima poseban duhovni autoritet.

sections.subtitle_en: Homework that changed a life: how Dave de la Cruz “Googled” Merz
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Nagy recounts how a young Filipino discovered Bl. Ivan Merz on the internet
sections.content_en:
Fr. Nagy emphasizes that no one from Croatia went to spread devotion to Merz to the Philippines. The story was told to him by **Dave de la Cruz** himself, an eighteen-year-old at the time. He was a good altar server, closely connected with the Church, so the parish priest sent him to a liturgical course in his city.

The professor gave the participants homework: to find saints on the internet especially connected with the liturgy. The obedient student typed “saints liturgy” into the search engine. As he later recounted, **the first name that appeared on the screen was Ivan Merz**. He had never heard of him.

The postulation already had a website back then and quite a few texts translated into English. The young man read everything and was thrilled, “something ignited in him”. He immediately contacted the postulation and asked for as much information as possible. They sent him pictures, holy cards, and second-class relics. With the help of his parents, who were better off financially, **in 2007 he traveled by plane to Zagreb to Merz's tomb**.

In Zagreb, he received additional information and literature. Upon his return, he founded a **youth association** that venerates the saints, and in a special way Bl. Ivan Merz. Today, the association has about **200 members** and has its own center, a house. Fr. Nagy notes that “we don't have something like that here yet”. In the house, there is a chapel of Bl. Ivan Merz with relics and pictures, “truly something incredible”. All of this can be seen on their website.

sections.subtitle: Vicepostulatura na Filipinima i 7000 potpisa za kanonizaciju
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o imenovanju Davea de la Cruza vicepostulatorom i prikupljanju potpisa za papu
sections.content:
Kad su u postulaturi vidjeli kako se štovanje širi, **Dave de la Cruz imenovan je vicepostulatorom**. U međuvremenu je završio studij teologije i filozofije, ali je ostao laik i pridružio se dominikanskom redu kao trećoredac. Prema crkvenim propisima, kako objašnjava p. Nagy, ondje gdje se štovanje širi izvan matične zemlje mora postojati vicepostulatura. Tako je ona osnovana i na Filipinima.

Filipinska mladež prošle je godine, kako gost kaže, „napravila čudo“ koje u Hrvatskoj nikome nije palo na pamet. Prikupili su **7000 potpisa** na molbu Svetom Ocu, novom papi, za proglašenje blaženika svetim. Molba je svečano predana Kongregaciji, a prefekt ju je predao papi, koji ju je primio i zahvalio. Voditelj dodaje da se sada čekaju odgovor i reakcija.

magisterium.assessment: Opis širenja pobožnosti prema bl. Ivanu Merzu, sudjelovanja laika i imenovanja vicepostulatora sam po sebi nije u proturječju s katoličkim naukom: postupak kanonizacije može uključivati laike, a vicepostulator može zamijeniti postulatora pod propisanim uvjetima. Ipak, tvrdnju da je vicepostulatura obvezna svugdje gdje se štovanje proširi izvan matične zemlje dostupni crkveni propisi ne potvrđuju, pa je treba provjeriti ili formulirati opreznije.
concerns: Navedeni propis kaže da postulator može imenovati vicepostulatora uz pisani mandat i prethodnu suglasnost podnositelja molbe; ne navodi da je vicepostulatura obvezna čim se pobožnost proširi u drugu zemlju. Zato je taj dio iskaza nedovoljno potkrijepljen, a može stvoriti pogrešan dojam o crkvenom postupku.
Odlomak je prekinut nakon riječi „prikupili“, pa se iz dostavljenog teksta ne može procijeniti tvrdnja o broju potpisa ni njezin kontekst.
magisterium.enrichment: Postulator i vicepostulator služe crkvenom ispitivanju života, kreposti, ugleda svetosti i mogućih znakova povezanih sa slugom Božjim; postupak zato nije samo promicanje popularnosti, nego pažljivo crkveno razlučivanje. Crkva pritom predlaže svece vjernicima kao uzore evanđeoskog života, a štovanje svetaca treba voditi Kristu i poticati vjernike da nasljeduju njihove kreposti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the spread of devotion to Bl. Ivan Merz, the participation of laypeople, and the appointment of a vice-postulator is not in itself contrary to Catholic teaching: the canonization process may include laypeople, and a vice-postulator may substitute for the postulator under prescribed conditions. Nevertheless, the claim that a vice-postulation is mandatory wherever veneration spreads outside the mother country is not confirmed by available church regulations, so it should be verified or formulated more cautiously.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The postulator and vice-postulator serve the ecclesial examination of the life, virtues, reputation of holiness, and possible signs associated with the Servant of God; the process is therefore not merely the promotion of popularity, but careful ecclesial discernment. concerns_en: The cited regulation states that the postulator may appoint a vice-postulator with a written mandate and the prior consent of the petitioner; it does not state that a vice-postulation is mandatory as soon as devotion spreads to another country. sections.subtitle_en: Vice-postulation in the Philippines and 7,000 Signatures for Canonization
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the appointment of Dave de la Cruz as vice-postulator and the gathering of signatures for the Pope
sections.content_en:
When they in the postulation saw how the veneration was spreading, **Dave de la Cruz was appointed vice-postulator**. In the meantime, he finished his studies in theology and philosophy, but remained a layman and joined the Dominican Order as a tertiary. According to church regulations, as Fr. Nagy explains, where veneration spreads outside the mother country, there must be a vice-postulation. Thus it was established in the Philippines as well.

Last year, Philippine youth, as the guest says, "worked a miracle" that occurred to no one in Croatia. They gathered **7,000 signatures** on a petition to the Holy Father, the new Pope, for the canonization of the blessed. The petition was solemnly submitted to the Congregation, and the prefect presented it to the Pope, who received it and gave thanks. The host adds that an answer and reaction are now awaited.

sections.subtitle: Vrhunac rada postulature i susret koji je premostio šest desetljeća
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy pripovijeda o otkriću sestre benediktinke na čijem je oblačenju 1921. bio Merz
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća da p. Nagy nije prvi, nego drugi postulator Merčeve kauze, te ga pita koji mu je trenutak bio najzanimljiviji. Gost kaže da je vrhunac svega bila **beatifikacija**, koju je dočekao nakon mnogo truda i rada. Kao osobno najdirljivije iskustvo ipak izdvaja jedno otkriće.

Kao student u Parizu Merz je **4. studenoga 1921.** prisustvovao oblačenju mlade djevojke koja je ulazila u benediktinski samostan. Bila je jedinica u obitelji i kći generala francuske vojske iz Prvog svjetskog rata. Sa 19 godina sve je ostavila i posvetila se Bogu. Duboko dirnut, Merz je iste večeri u dnevnik zapisao dojmove: **„Danas sam sudjelovao na oblačenju jedne sestre novakinje benediktinke. Liturgija veličajna. Djevojka ostavlja svijet, ulazi da se potpuno posveti Bogu.“** P. Nagy taj prekrasni opis preporučuje svima.

Ime djevojke Merz nije zapisao. Ostavio je samo tri podatka: samostan sestara benediktinki u ulici **Rue Monsieur**, datum i to da je djevojka kći francuskog generala.

P. Nagy postao je postulator **1972.** Godine 1979. s petoricom kolega boravio je tri mjeseca u Parizu na takozvanoj trećoj probaciji, završnoj formaciji isusovačkog reda. Prvog slobodnog dana otišao je u spomenutu ulicu, ali samostana više nije bilo. Rekli su mu da je prestao postojati 1939. Sestre su se, zbog neriješenih vlasničkih odnosa, preselile u novi samostan nekih 15 km od Pariza (u transkriptu zabilježen kao Boileau-Nocaze) i dali mu broj telefona.

Nakon ručka nazvao je samostan. Sestri vratarici predstavio se kao isusovac iz Hrvatske i iznio tri podatka. Voditelj napominje da je otada prošlo gotovo 60 godina, a između je bio i Drugi svjetski rat. Vratarica je otišla pitati sestre okupljene na rekreaciji poslije ručka. Nakon tri minute vratila se riječima: **„Pater, imate nevjerojatnu sreću.“** Sestra je bila živa i među njima. Zvala se **Marie-Denise Chaville** i jedina je toga dana ušla u samostan, a otac joj je bio general.

P. Nagyju su, kako priznaje, od ganuća gotovo došle suze. Imao je dojam da se preselio pedeset godina unatrag. Poručio je sestri da će za nekoliko dana doći isusovac iz Hrvatske i donijeti joj opis njezina oblačenja kako ga je doživio jedan mladi hrvatski student. Tekst je dao prevesti i posjetio je. Bio je to, kaže, izvanredno dirljiv susret. Sestra dotad nikad nije čula za Merza, a cijeli ga je samostan potom prihvatio. Njezin je život tekao upravo onako kako je Merz gotovo proročki predvidio. Umrla je oko **1989.** u dubokoj starosti, s 90 godina. P. Nagy bio je na njezinu sprovodu jer je tada ponovno služio u Parizu.

magisterium.assessment: U dostavljenom izvatku nema teološke tvrdnje koja bi proturječila katoličkom nauku: beatifikacija i redovničko posvećenje prikazani su pozitivno, a dirljivi susret kao osobno svjedočanstvo. Budući da se odlomak prekida usred rečenice, pojedinosti o redovnici i susretu ne mogu se potpuno provjeriti ni vrednovati u širem kontekstu.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni prikaz Ivana Merza potvrđuje da je studirao u Parizu te ističe njegov rast u vjeri, liturgijski život i apostolat među mladima kao važne sastavnice njegova svjedočanstva. Anegdota o susretu može potaknuti promišljanje o redovničkom pozivu, ali sama po sebi nije teološki nauk niti dokaz o povijesnim pojedinostima.
magisterium.assessment_en: In the provided excerpt, there is no theological claim that would contradict Catholic teaching: beatification and religious consecration are presented positively, and the touching encounter as a personal testimony. Since the passage breaks off mid-sentence, the details about the religious sister and the encounter cannot be fully verified or evaluated in a broader context.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church's account of Ivan Merz confirms that he studied in Paris and highlights his growth in faith, liturgical life, and apostolate among young people as important components of his testimony. The anecdote about the encounter may stimulate reflection on the religious vocation, but in itself is neither theological teaching nor proof of historical details.

sections.subtitle_en: The culmination of the postulation's work and an encounter that bridged six decades
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Nagy recounts the discovery of the Benedictine sister at whose clothing Merz was present in 1921
sections.content_en:
The host reminds that Fr. Nagy is not the first, but the second postulator of Merz's cause, and asks him which moment was the most interesting to him. The guest says that the culmination of everything was the **beatification**, which he lived to see after much effort and work. As his personally most touching experience, he nevertheless singles out one discovery.

As a student in Paris, on **November 4, 1921**, Merz attended the clothing of a young girl who was entering a Benedictine monastery. She was an only child in the family and the daughter of a French army general from the First World War. At 19 years old, she left everything and consecrated herself to God. Deeply moved, Merz wrote down his impressions in his diary that same evening: **“Today I took part in the clothing of a Benedictine novice sister. The liturgy magnificent. The girl leaves the world, enters to consecrate herself completely to God.”** Fr. Nagy recommends this wonderful description to everyone.

Merz did not write down the girl's name. He left only three pieces of information: the monastery of the Benedictine sisters on **Rue Monsieur**, the date, and that the girl was the daughter of a French general.

Fr. Nagy became postulator in **1972**. In 1979, with five colleagues, he stayed for three months in Paris on the so-called third probation, the final formation of the Jesuit order. On the first free day, he went to the mentioned street, but the monastery was no longer there. They told him that it had ceased to exist in 1939. Due to unresolved property relations, the sisters moved to a new monastery some 15 km from Paris (recorded in the transcript as Boileau-Nocaze), and they gave him the phone number.

After lunch, he called the monastery. He introduced himself to the sister portress as a Jesuit from Croatia and presented the three pieces of information. The host notes that nearly 60 years had passed since then, and in between was also the Second World War. The portress went to ask the sisters gathered for recreation after lunch. After three minutes, she returned with the words: **“Father, you are incredibly lucky.”** The sister was alive and among them. Her name was **Marie-Denise Chaville**, and she was the only one who entered the monastery that day, and her father was a general.

Tears almost came to Fr. Nagy's eyes from emotion, as he admits. He had the impression that he had moved fifty years back. He sent word to the sister that in a few days a Jesuit from Croatia would come and bring her the description of her clothing as experienced by a young Croatian student. He had the text translated and visited her. It was, he says, an extraordinarily touching encounter. Until then, the sister had never heard of Merz, and the entire monastery subsequently accepted him. Her life unfolded exactly as Merz had almost prophetically predicted. She died around **1989** at an advanced age, at 90 years old. Fr. Nagy was at her funeral because he was serving in Paris again at that time.

sections.subtitle: Živa svjedočanstva i srećka koja je platila grob na Mirogoju
sections.screenshot_description: Gost pripovijeda o lutrijskoj srećki pronađenoj u Merčevu novčaniku
sections.content:
P. Nagy dodaje da je tijekom rada na beatifikaciji susreo mnoge ljude koji su Merza osobno poznavali i dali o njemu prekrasna svjedočanstva. Sva su snimljena, zapisana i sačuvana. Voditelj to opisuje kao velik posao i istodobno „vremeplov u prošlost“.

Gost zatim govori o uslišanjima. Zabilježeno ih je **oko 600 raznih vrsta**. Posebno ističe ona za koja se nitko nije molio, nego je blaženik, kako kaže, sam intervenirao, i to za vlastiti grob.

Merz je najprije pokopan na **Mirogoju**. Nekoliko dana nakon sinove smrti otac je raspremao njegove stvari i u novčaniku, koji se i danas čuva u Merčevu muzeju, pronašao **lutrijsku srećku**. Izvlačenje je bilo zakazano za kraj svibnja 1928. Otac ju je za svaki slučaj sačuvao. Srećka je dobila **750 tadašnjih jugoslavenskih dinara**, točno onoliko koliko je otac platio grobno mjesto na Mirogoju. Voditelj kaže da mu je ta zgoda već bila poznata.

magisterium.assessment: Opis je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkom vjerom: štovanje blaženoga Ivana Merza i svjedočanstva o primljenim milostima mogu biti izraz vjere u zagovor svetih, a Crkva je Merza proglasila blaženim zbog njegova kršćanskog života usmjerenog Kristu. Ipak, tvrdnju da je blaženik „sam intervenirao” treba razumjeti kao njegov zagovor, a ne kao djelovanje neovisno o Bogu; sama brojka od oko 600 uslišanja ne potvrđuje da je svako od njih čudo.
concerns: Izraz „blaženik sam intervenirao” može zamagliti razliku između zagovora svetaca i Boga kao izvora milosti; bilo bi teološki preciznije reći da je Merz zagovarao pred Bogom.

Broj zabilježenih uslišanja i anegdota o srećki sami po sebi ne dokazuju nadnaravno djelovanje niti da je baš ono prouzročilo ishod. Za procjenu navodnih nadnaravnih pojava važni su, među ostalim, vjerodostojnost svjedoka, pravovjernost i duhovni plodovi.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk razlikuje Božje čudo od providonosne milosti ili uslišanja koja se mogu doživjeti kao posebna pomoć, ali se ne mogu sa sigurnošću proglasiti čudom. Govor o Merzovu zagovoru najjasniji je kada istodobno čuva tu razliku i usmjerava pažnju na Krista: u homiliji beatifikacije Merz je predstavljen kao uzor jer je nastojao biti sjedinjen s Bogom i služiti Kristu.
