magisterium.assessment_en: The description is generally aligned with the Catholic faith: veneration of Blessed Ivan Merz and testimonies of received graces can be an expression of faith in the intercession of the saints, and the Church beatified Merz because of his Christian life centered on Christ. However, the claim that the blessed "intervened himself" should be understood as his intercession, and not as an action independent of God; the figure of about 600 answered prayers alone does not confirm that each of them is a miracle.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching distinguishes God's miracle from providential grace or answered prayers that can be experienced as special help, but cannot be declared a miracle with certainty. Speaking of Merz's intercession is clearest when it simultaneously preserves that distinction and directs attention to Christ: in the beatification homily, Merz was presented as a role model because he sought to be united with God and to serve Christ.
concerns_en: The expression "the blessed intervened himself" may blur the distinction between the intercession of the saints and God as the source of grace; it would be theologically more precise to say that Merz interceded before God.

The number of recorded answered prayers and the anecdote about the lottery ticket do not in themselves prove supernatural action nor that it specifically caused the outcome. For the evaluation of alleged supernatural phenomena, among other things, the credibility of witnesses, orthodoxy, and spiritual fruits are important.

sections.subtitle_en: Living testimonies and the lottery ticket that paid for the grave at Mirogoj
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest recounts the lottery ticket found in Merz's wallet
sections.content_en:
Fr. Nagy adds that during his work on the beatification he met many people who knew Merz personally and gave wonderful testimonies about him. All of them were recorded, written down, and preserved. The host describes this as great work and at the same time a "time machine into the past".

The guest then speaks about answered prayers. **About 600 of various kinds** have been recorded. He particularly highlights those for which no one prayed, but rather the blessed, as he says, intervened himself, and that for his own grave.

Merz was first buried at **Mirogoj**. A few days after his son's death, the father was sorting through his belongings and in the wallet, which is kept to this day in the Merz museum, found a **lottery ticket**. The drawing was scheduled for the end of May 1928. The father kept it just in case. The ticket won **750 then-Yugoslav dinars**, exactly as much as the father had paid for the grave plot at Mirogoj. The host says that this incident was already familiar to him.

sections.subtitle: Prazna blagajna i neočekivani donator: kako je blaženik „sam platio“ novi grob
sections.screenshot_description: P. Nagy opisuje trenutak kada je nepoznati gospodin položio novac za grob na stol
sections.content:
Druga slična zgoda dogodila se pri prijenosu Merčevih posmrtnih ostataka s Mirogoja u **Baziliku Srca Isusova u Zagrebu** u prosincu 1977. Grob je iskopan na desnoj strani bazilike, kod oltara sv. Alojzija. Zidarski radovi bili su zahtjevni i stajali su blizu **900.000 tadašnjih dinara**, točnije 880.000 prema računu.

Nakon nekoliko dana, u petak, zidar je došao po isplatu, a blagajna postulature bila je potpuno prazna. P. Nagy, tada vjeroučitelj u Palmotićevoj, upravo se spremao s mladima na susret s mladim Slovencima. Zamolio je zidara da dođe u ponedjeljak. U sebi je već računao da će morati otići poglavaru i posuditi novac.

U ponedjeljak se zidar nije pojavio. Poslijepodne je iz župnog ureda nazvao kolega **p. Lozuk**: došao je neki gospodin u vezi s grobom i nekim novcem. P. Nagy je pomislio da je riječ o zidaru i predložio da dođe sutradan. Kolega ga je ispravio: gospodin nije došao po novac, nego ga *dati*. „Pa ako je za dat, nek dođe“, odgovorio je.

Došao je gospodin nižeg rasta, kako ga gost opisuje, „vrlo produhovljen“. Rekao je da je osobno poznavao Merza i bio u **orlovskoj organizaciji**, te da želi financijski pridonijeti uređenju groba. P. Nagy mu je iskreno priznao da ni dotadašnji radovi još nisu plaćeni. Gospodin je pogledao račun, pregledao stavke, rekao „U redu“, otvorio novčanik i na stol položio **900.000 dinara**.

„Ostao sam bez teksta“, prisjeća se p. Nagy. Na pitanje zašto je došao baš tada, donator je odgovorio da je dobio poticaj da mora nešto učiniti za blaženog Merza. Sutradan prijepodne zidar je bio isplaćen, ne sluteći ništa o tome što se dogodilo. Voditelj zaključuje: **„Blaženi Merz se opet pobrinuo za svoje.“** P. Nagy dodaje, uz smijeh, da se raspričao i da ga je voditelj trebao prekinuti.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: opisuje prijenos posmrtnih ostataka i financijsku poteškoću, bez izravne tvrdnje koja bi proturječila vjeri ili Svetom pismu. Budući da se tekst prekida prije raspleta, ne može se procijeniti znači li izraz „sam platio” pobožnu interpretaciju događaja ili tvrdnju o posebnom nadnaravnom zahvatu.
concerns: Ako se nastavak predstavlja kao dokaz da je blaženik nadnaravno pribavio novac, trebalo bi razlikovati pobožno tumačenje događaja od činjenice utvrđene crkvenim postupkom; sam odlomak ne daje dovoljno podataka za takvu procjenu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička vjera ispovijeda Božju providnost kao Božje brižno čuvanje i upravljanje stvorenjem, ali to ne znači da svaki neočekivani događaj treba bez daljnjeg proglasiti čudom. Službeni dokument o beatifikaciji potvrđuje da se Merčev grob nalazi u zagrebačkoj bazilici Srca Isusova, ali ne potvrđuje ovu pojedinačnu zgodu s troškom radova.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it describes the transfer of mortal remains and a financial difficulty, without any direct assertion that would contradict the faith or Sacred Scripture. Since the text breaks off before the resolution, it cannot be assessed whether the expression „paid for himself” means a pious interpretation of the event or an assertion of a special supernatural intervention.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic faith professes Divine Providence as God's caring preservation and governance of creation, but that does not mean that every unexpected event should be declared a miracle without further ado. The official beatification document confirms that Merz's tomb is located in the Zagreb Bazilika Srca Isusova, but it does not confirm this individual incident regarding the cost of the work.
concerns_en: If the continuation is presented as proof that the blessed supernaturally obtained the money, a pious interpretation of the event should be distinguished from a fact established by ecclesial procedure; the passage itself does not provide enough data for such an assessment.

sections.subtitle_en: An empty cashbox and an unexpected donor: how the blessed "paid for" the new tomb himself
sections.screenshot_description_en: P. Nagy describes the moment when an unknown gentleman placed the money for the tomb on the table
sections.content_en:
Another similar incident occurred during the transfer of Merz's mortal remains from Mirogoj to the **Bazilika Srca Isusova in Zagreb** in December 1977. The tomb was dug on the right side of the basilica, by the altar of Saint Aloysius. The masonry work was demanding and cost nearly **900,000 dinars of that time**, more precisely 880,000 according to the bill.

After a few days, on Friday, the mason came for payment, and the postulation's cashbox was completely empty. P. Nagy, then a catechist in Palmotićeva, was just preparing to go with the young people to a meeting with young Slovenians. He asked the mason to come on Monday. Inwardly, he was already calculating that he would have to go to the superior and borrow money.

On Monday the mason did not show up. In the afternoon, colleague **p. Lozuk** called from the parish office: a gentleman had arrived in connection with the tomb and some money. P. Nagy thought that it was the mason and suggested that he come the next day. His colleague corrected him: the gentleman had not come for money, but to *give* it. „Well, if it is to give, let him come,” he replied.

A gentleman of shorter stature arrived, as the guest describes him, „very spiritual.” He said that he personally knew Merz and had been in the **Orlovska organizacija**, and that he wanted to contribute financially to the arrangement of the tomb. P. Nagy honestly admitted to him that even the work done so far had not yet been paid for. The gentleman looked at the bill, reviewed the items, said „All right,” opened his wallet, and placed **900,000 dinars** on the table.

„I was left speechless,” recalls P. Nagy. When asked why he had come precisely then, the donor replied that he had received an inspiration that he had to do something for Blessed Merz. The next morning the mason was paid, suspecting nothing of what had happened. The host concludes: **„Blessed Merz took care of his own again.”** P. Nagy adds, with a laugh, that he had talked too much and that the host should have interrupted him.

sections.subtitle: Vjera koja se ne skriva: Merz i javno svjedočenje
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pita p. Božidara Nagyja kako bi blaženi Ivan Merz gledao na javnu molitvu krunice
sections.content:
Nakon niza anegdota iz rada postulature, p. Božidar Nagy u šali primjećuje da se previše raspričao i da ga je voditelj trebao prekinuti. Voditelj odgovara da mu je bilo žao to učiniti. Zatim prelazi na pitanje koje je zajednici okupljenoj oko podcasta posebno blisko: **kako je Ivan Merz gledao na javno svjedočenje vjere** i što bi mislio o javnoj molitvi krunice.

Odgovor je jednoznačan. Merz je, ističe p. Nagy, *i te kako* bio za javno svjedočenje vjere. Kao dokaz navodi jedno njegovo „čuveno pismo”, objavljeno u Merzovim Sabranim djelima. Odmah zatim uzima sedmi svezak koji je voditelj imao pri ruci (on kaže da su „svi tu”) i počinje tražiti ulomak. Pritom napominje da se to isplati jer je riječ o „tako zanimljivom tekstu”.

Traženje traje nekoliko trenutaka. Prvo nailazi na pismo koje je Merz iz Pariza uputio roditeljima, a zatim pronalazi pravo: pismo profesoru **Ljubomiru Marakoviću**, s kojim je Merz vodio intenzivnu prepisku.

magisterium.assessment: Tvrdnja da je Merz podupirao javno svjedočenje vjere načelno je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: kršćani su pozvani svjedočiti Kristu riječju i životom, bez stida i uz poštovanje drugih. Ipak, izvadak prekida prije nego što iznese najavljeni dokaz, pa se ovdje ne može provjeriti koliko je povijesna tvrdnja o Merzovu stavu — niti njezina primjena na javnu molitvu krunice — potkrijepljena.
concerns: Izvadak ne sadrži najavljeni dokaz o Merzovu stavu, pa se povijesna atribucija ne može potvrditi samo na temelju dostavljenog teksta.
Nije razjašnjeno razlikuje li se javno svjedočenje vjere od pritiska ili nametanja; katoličko svjedočenje treba biti jasno, ali ne smije postati prisila ili propaganda.
magisterium.enrichment: Katekizam uči da kršćanin u okolnostima koje traže svjedočenje treba ispovjediti vjeru bez dvosmislenosti, a Isusove riječi o svjetlu svijeta povezuju svjedočanstvo s vidljivim životom učenika (Mt 5,16). To svjedočenje treba davati s blagošću i poštovanjem te bez pritiska na druge; zato se javna molitva može razumjeti kao oblik vjerskog svjedočenja, ali njezina konkretna primjerenost ovisi i o načinu na koji se provodi.

citations.document_title: Christian witness in a multi-religious world

magisterium.assessment_en: The claim that Merz supported the public witness of faith is in principle aligned with Catholic teaching: Christians are called to witness to Christ by word and life, without shame and with respect for others. However, the excerpt cuts off before presenting the announced proof, so it cannot be verified here how well the historical claim about Merz's stance — or its application to the public prayer of the Rosary — is supported.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catechism teaches that a Christian, in circumstances that require witness, must profess the faith without ambiguity, and Jesus' words about the light of the world connect witness with the visible life of the disciples (Mt 5:16). This witness should be given with gentleness and respect, and without pressure on others; therefore, public prayer can be understood as a form of religious witness, but its concrete appropriateness also depends on the manner in which it is conducted.
concerns_en: The excerpt does not contain the announced proof of Merz's stance, so the historical attribution cannot be confirmed solely on the basis of the provided text.
It is not clarified whether the public witness of faith is distinguished from pressure or imposition; Catholic witness should be clear, but must not become coercion or propaganda.

sections.subtitle_en: A Faith That Does Not Hide: Merz and Public Witness
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks p. Božidar Nagy how Blessed Ivan Merz would view the public prayer of the Rosary
sections.content_en:
After a series of anecdotes from the work of the postulation, p. Božidar Nagy jokingly remarks that he talked too much and that the host should have interrupted him. The host replies that he was sorry to do so. Then he moves on to a question that is especially close to the community gathered around the podcast: **how Ivan Merz viewed the public witness of faith** and what he would think about the public prayer of the Rosary.

The answer is unequivocal. Merz was, p. Nagy emphasizes, *very much* in favor of the public witness of faith. As proof, he cites one of his “famous letters”, published in Merz's Collected Works. Immediately after, he takes the seventh volume that the host had at hand (he says that “they are all here”) and begins looking for the excerpt. At the same time, he notes that it is worth it because it is “such an interesting text”.

The search lasts a few moments. First he comes across a letter that Merz sent to his parents from Paris, and then he finds the right one: a letter to Professor **Ljubomir Maraković**, with whom Merz carried on an intensive correspondence.

sections.subtitle: „Na nama je krivnja”: oštro pismo iz Pariza
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy čita naglas Merzovo pismo Marakoviću iz sedmog sveska Sabranih djela
sections.content:
Prema uvodnoj bilješci koju p. Nagy čita, Merz u tom pismu svome profesoru Marakoviću iznosi **apostolski program** koji želi ostvarivati u domovini nakon povratka sa studija u Parizu. Najvažniji dio nalazi se na kraju pisma, a p. Nagy ga čita u cijelosti:

> „Iako katolicizam u Europi sada raste, ipak je u užasnoj regresiji. I spoznavši, osjetivši u Lurdu upravo na silan način da je cijelo čovječanstvo ta mrvica stvorena da odaje poštovanje neizmjernom Bogu, a kad tamo države, zakoni, radnici, zidari, cijeli činovnički aparat funkcionira kao mašina, kao da Bog ne postoji. Čovjeku se zgrozi kad to pomisli. A tko je kriv? Dobri, jer nisu bolji.”

Merz zatim nastavlja i krivnju ne pripisuje svijetu, nego samim vjernicima:

> „Čovječanstvo jednostavno ne zna da Bog postoji, jer katolici, mjesto da se mole na javnim mjestima, mjesto da napuste svaki položaj ako je u protuslovlju s vjerom, oni se sakriju kad se Bogu mole, pričešćuju kad nije nitko u crkvi. Na nama je krivnja.”

Pismo završava usporedbom s prvim kršćanima. Oni su u odnosu na rimsku religiju bili „tako zvani veleizdajnici”, u opoziciji prema poganskoj državi i okolini, te su bili bičevani i bacani u tamnice. Današnji kršćani, piše Merz, „zašute čim vide opasnost”.

Voditelj nakon čitanja kratko zaključuje da je time sve rečeno. P. Nagy se slaže: stav je izrečen posve jasno. Dodaje da bi se Merz, kad bi danas živio i čuo za molitelje krunice na javnim mjestima, „među prvima” pridružio. Voditelj nadovezuje da bi takvu inicijativu možda i sam pokrenuo, što p. Nagy potvrđuje.

magisterium.assessment: Vidljivi dio odlomka uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim naukom: javno svjedočenje vjere i nastojanje da se Krist ne skriva podudaraju se s pozivom učenika da vjeru ispovijedaju i svjedoče za nju. Ipak, citat je prekinut, pa se ne može pouzdano ocijeniti što Merz zaključuje o državama i zakonima niti je li tvrdnju o „krivnji” razradio s potrebnim nijansama.
concerns: Izvadak ne donosi cijeli citat, pa je procjena njegova završnog argumenta i značenja izraza „na nama je krivnja” nužno ograničena.

Tvrdnja o katolicizmu koji istodobno raste i prolazi „užasnu regresiju” nije u prikazanom odlomku obrazložena; bez dodatnog konteksta nije jasno govori li Merz o brojčanom rastu, javnom utjecaju ili životu vjere.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk razlikuje unutarnju vjeru od njezina svjedočenja: vjera treba oblikovati život, a kršćanin je, kada okolnosti to zahtijevaju, treba ispovjediti i riječima; Isusov poziv da ga priznamo pred ljudima nalazi se u Mt 10,32–33. Javno svjedočenje pritom nije prisila ni puko političko nadmetanje, nego vjerno življenje i naviještanje evanđelja uz poštovanje drugih.
magisterium.assessment_en: The visible part of the excerpt is generally in accordance with Catholic teaching: public witness of faith and the effort not to hide Christ coincide with the call of disciples to profess the faith and witness to it. Nevertheless, the quote is cut off, so it cannot be reliably assessed what Merz concludes about states and laws, nor whether he elaborated the claim about „guilt” with the necessary nuances.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching distinguishes interior faith from its witness: faith should shape life, and a Christian, when circumstances require it, should profess it also in words; Jesus' call to acknowledge him before men is found in Mt 10:32–33. Public witness is thereby neither coercion nor mere political competition, but the faithful living and proclaiming of the Gospel with respect for others.
concerns_en: The excerpt does not provide the entire quote, so the assessment of its concluding argument and the meaning of the expression „the guilt is on us” is necessarily limited.

The claim about Catholicism simultaneously growing and undergoing a „terrible regression” is not substantiated in the presented excerpt; without additional context, it is not clear whether Merz is speaking about numerical growth, public influence, or the life of faith.

sections.subtitle_en: „The guilt is on us”: a sharp letter from Paris
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy reads aloud Merz's letter to Maraković from the seventh volume of the Collected Works
sections.content_en:
According to the introductory note that Fr. Nagy reads, Merz in that letter presents to his professor Maraković an **apostolic program** that he wants to realize in the homeland after returning from studies in Paris. The most important part is at the end of the letter, and Fr. Nagy reads it in its entirety:

> „Although Catholicism in Europe is now growing, it is nevertheless in terrible regression. And having realized, having felt in Lourdes precisely in a powerful way that all of humanity is that crumb created to pay homage to the immense God, and yet states, laws, workers, masons, the entire bureaucratic apparatus functions like a machine, as if God does not exist. One is appalled when one thinks of this. And who is to blame? The good, because they are not better.”

Merz then continues and does not attribute the guilt to the world, but to the believers themselves:

> „Humanity simply does not know that God exists, because Catholics, instead of praying in public places, instead of abandoning every position if it is in contradiction with the faith, they hide when they pray to God, receive Communion when no one is in church. The guilt is on us.”

The letter ends with a comparison to the early Christians. In relation to Roman religion, they were „so-called traitors”, in opposition to the pagan state and environment, and they were scourged and thrown into dungeons. Today's Christians, Merz writes, „fall silent as soon as they see danger”.

After the reading, the host briefly concludes that everything has been said with that. Fr. Nagy agrees: the stance was expressed quite clearly. He adds that Merz, if he were alive today and heard of the Rosary pray-ers in public places, would join „among the first”. The host adds that he might have launched such an initiative himself, which Fr. Nagy confirms.

sections.subtitle: Dvaput dnevno s krunicom preko Trga bana Jelačića
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy opisuje Merzov svakodnevni put preko Trga bana Jelačića s krunicom u džepu
sections.content:
Merz o javnoj molitvi nije samo pisao, nego ju je i živio. P. Nagy otkriva detalj iz njegove zagrebačke svakodnevice. Merz je stanovao blizu kolodvora, u **Starčevićevu domu**, a radio je na **Kaptolu**, u gimnaziji. Zato je **svaki dan dvaput prelazio Trg bana Jelačića s krunicom u džepu** i molio je na putu na posao i s posla.

Voditelj u tome prepoznaje izravnu poveznicu s današnjom praksom javne molitve na glavnom zagrebačkom trgu. Merz je, kaže voditelj, svojom molitvom krunice praktički posvećivao Trg. Upravo to danas čine molitelji koji ondje zazivaju Gospu i njezin blagoslov. P. Nagy dodaje da je riječ o istom načelu iz pisma: moliti se na javnim mjestima. Voditelj taj dio razgovora zaključuje riječju „predivno”.

magisterium.assessment: Opis svakodnevne molitve krunice i njezina povezivanja vjere sa svakodnevnim životom u skladu je s katoličkom pobožnošću: krunica je biblijski nadahnuta, usredotočena na Kristova otajstva i preporučena kao osobna i zajednička molitva. Usporedbu s današnjom javnom molitvom valja razumjeti kao sličnost u javnom svjedočenju vjere, a ne kao tvrdnju da su osobna molitva u hodu i organizirana javna pobožnost istovjetne.
concerns: Povijesni navod da je Merz svakodnevno molio krunicu upravo na putu preko Trga bana Jelačića ne može se provjeriti na temelju dostupnih izvora; to je pitanje povijesne točnosti, a ne samo po sebi teološki problem.
Ne bi trebalo iz primjera zaključiti da je javno moljenje krunice obvezno za sve vjernike ili da je jedini vrijedan oblik javnog svjedočenja vjere.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva krunicu opisuje kao molitvu koja vodi razmatranju spasenjskih događaja Kristova života u povezanosti s Marijom, pa njezino moljenje može pomagati da se vjera prenese u svakodnevno djelovanje. Istodobno, krunica je pobožna praksa, a ne liturgija, i treba je razlikovati od liturgijskog slavlja; Crkva je preporučuje, ali vjernik treba biti slobodan prihvatiti je bez nametanja krivnje onima koji je ne mole redovito.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the daily prayer of the Rosary and its linking of faith with everyday life is in accordance with Catholic piety: the Rosary is biblically inspired, centered on the mysteries of Christ, and recommended as personal and communal prayer. The comparison with today's public prayer should be understood as a similarity in the public witnessing of faith, and not as an assertion that personal prayer while walking and organized public devotion are identical.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church describes the Rosary as a prayer that leads to the contemplation of the salvific events of Christ's life in connection with Mary, so praying it can help translate faith into daily action. At the same time, the Rosary is a pious practice, not liturgy, and should be distinguished from liturgical celebration; the Church recommends it, but the faithful should be free to accept it without imposing guilt on those who do not pray it regularly.
concerns_en: The historical statement that Merz prayed the Rosary daily precisely on his way across Trg bana Jelačića cannot be verified based on available sources; this is a question of historical accuracy, not a theological problem in itself.
One should not conclude from the example that the public praying of the Rosary is obligatory for all faithful or that it is the only valuable form of public witnessing of faith.

sections.subtitle_en: Twice a day with the Rosary across Trg bana Jelačića
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy describes Merz's daily route across Trg bana Jelačića with the Rosary in his pocket
sections.content_en:
Merz did not only write about public prayer, but he also lived it. Fr. Nagy reveals a detail from his Zagreb everyday life. Merz lived near the station, in **Starčevićev dom**, and worked at **Kaptol**, in the gymnasium. That is why **every day he crossed Trg bana Jelačića twice with the Rosary in his pocket** and prayed it on the way to and from work.

The host recognizes in this a direct connection with today's practice of public prayer on Zagreb's main square. Merz, says the host, practically sanctified the Square with his Rosary prayer. That is precisely what the pray-ers do today who invoke Our Lady and her blessing there. Fr. Nagy adds that it is the same principle from the letter: to pray in public places. The host concludes that part of the conversation with the word "wonderful".

sections.subtitle: Čudo iz 2018. čeka u Vatikanu: kako izgleda put do kanonizacije
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy objašnjava postupak priznavanja čuda pred trima komisijama
sections.content:
Na pitanje kada će Merz biti proglašen svetim, p. Nagy ne daje datum, ali izražava nadu. Hrvatska strana, kaže, ispunila je sve uvjete. Sva dokumentacija o **čudu koje se 2018. godine dogodilo na Merzovu grobu** predana je **Dikasteriju za kauze svetaca**, gdje sada čeka u redu da bude uzeta na proučavanje.

P. Nagy zatim objašnjava kojim putem svako čudo mora proći. Ono mora dobiti odobrenje **triju komisija**:

- **Liječnička komisija**: hrvatski liječnici već su sve odobrili (p. Nagy usput spominje da je bilo „zanimljivo kako je to išlo”), a sada slučaj moraju pregledati vatikanski liječnici.
- **Teološka komisija**: teolozi utvrđuju je li čudesno ozdravljenje doista povezano s blaženim Merzom, odnosno s njegovim zagovorom i posredovanjem.
- **Komisija biskupa i kardinala**: prema riječima p. Nagyja, ovaj je korak „više-manje formalan”.

Kada sve bude završeno, izdaje se **dekret o čudu**, čime se otvara „zeleno svjetlo” za kanonizaciju. Nakon toga je na mjesnoj Crkvi da se s papom dogovori kada će i gdje kanonizacija biti održana.

magisterium.assessment: Opis glavnih faza ispitivanja navodnog čuda uglavnom je usklađen s crkvenim postupkom: medicinska procjena slijedi se teološkim razmatranjem, a potom razmatranjem kardinala i biskupa. Ipak, tvrdnju da su hrvatski liječnici već sve odobrili valja razlikovati od službene procjene Medicinskog kolegija Dikasterija, a iz ovog odlomka nije moguće potvrditi pojedinosti slučaja iz 2018.
concerns: Izraz „triju komisija” razumljivo sažima tri razine razmatranja, ali može ostaviti pogrešan dojam da su sve tri formalno liječničke ili istovrsne komisije; službeni opis navodi sastanak medicinskih stručnjaka, posebni sastanak teologa te sjednicu kardinala i biskupa.

Odobrenje liječnika u Hrvatskoj samo po sebi ne znači da je čudo priznato u crkvenom postupku: medicinska procjena u Dikasteriju zasebna je stručna faza. Dok postupak nije zaključen, preciznije je govoriti o navodnom ili mogućem čudu.
Odlomak ne iznosi izričitu tvrdnju o biblijskom nauku, pa se njegova biblijska usklađenost ne može posebno procijeniti na temelju dostupnog sadržaja.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva u postupku ne poistovjećuje medicinsku neobjašnjivost s konačnim priznanjem čuda: medicinski stručnjaci procjenjuju ozdravljenje prema znanstvenim mjerilima, dok teološka prosudba razmatra njegovo značenje u vjeri i povezanost s kandidatom za kanonizaciju. Papa Benedikt XVI. naglasio je da se stručna i teološka procjena nadopunjuju, pri čemu se medicinska prosudba nastavlja teološkim ispitivanjem i odlukom crkvenih vlasti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the main stages of examining an alleged miracle is generally aligned with the Church's procedure: a medical evaluation is followed by theological examination, and then by the consideration of cardinals and bishops. However, the claim that Croatian doctors have already approved everything should be distinguished from the official assessment of the Medical Board of the Dicastery, and from this excerpt it is not possible to confirm the details of the 2018 case.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In the process, the Church does not equate medical inexplicability with the definitive recognition of a miracle: medical experts evaluate the healing according to scientific criteria, while theological judgment examines its significance in faith and connection to the candidate for canonization. Pope Benedict XVI emphasized that the expert and theological evaluations complement each other, with the medical judgment being followed by theological examination and the decision of ecclesiastical authorities.
concerns_en: The expression “three commissions” understandably summarizes the three levels of consideration, but it may leave the false impression that all three are formally medical or identical types of commissions; the official description lists a meeting of medical experts, a special meeting of theologians, and an ordinary session of cardinals and bishops.

Approval by doctors in Croatia does not in itself mean that the miracle is recognized in the ecclesiastical procedure: the medical evaluation in the Dicastery is a separate expert stage. Until the procedure is concluded, it is more precise to speak of an alleged or possible miracle.
The excerpt does not make an explicit claim about biblical teaching, so its biblical alignment cannot be specifically evaluated based on the available content.

sections.subtitle_en: The 2018 miracle waits in the Vatican: what the path to canonization looks like
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy explains the procedure for recognizing a miracle before three commissions
sections.content_en:
To the question of when Merz will be declared a saint, Fr. Nagy does not give a date, but expresses hope. The Croatian side, he says, has fulfilled all conditions. All documentation about the **miracle that occurred in 2018 at Merz's tomb** has been submitted to the **Dicastery for the Causes of Saints**, where it is now waiting in line to be taken up for study.

Fr. Nagy then explains which path every miracle must take. It must receive the approval of **three commissions**:

- **Medical Commission**: Croatian doctors have already approved everything (Fr. Nagy mentions in passing that it was “interesting how that went”), and now the case must be examined by Vatican doctors.
- **Theological Commission**: theologians determine whether the miraculous healing is indeed connected with Blessed Merz, that is, with his intercession and mediation.
- **Commission of Bishops and Cardinals**: according to Fr. Nagy, this step is “more or less formal”.

When everything is completed, a **decree on the miracle** is issued, opening the “green light” for canonization. After that, it is up to the local Church to agree with the pope when and where the canonization will be held.

sections.subtitle: Slika predana papi i molitva svakog desetog u mjesecu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj pripovijeda o predaji slike blaženog Ivana Merza papi u Rimu
sections.content:
Voditelj podsjeća na tisuće potpisa koje je mladež s Filipina uputila Svetom Ocu i u šali kaže da se novog papu „bombardira Merzom”. I njegova je zajednica tome pridonijela. Ove su godine imali, kako kaže, „priliku i čast i milost” biti u Rimu **25. ožujka, na svetkovinu Navještenja Blažene Djevice Marije**, i papi predati sliku blaženog Ivana Merza. Uz sliku su priložili molbu da se njihov zaštitnik što prije proglasi svetim. Kopiju slike namjeravaju izraditi i za sebe.

P. Nagy ističe da to iščekuju svi Merzovi štovatelji i da za tu nakanu treba moliti. U **Bazilici Srca Isusova** u Zagrebu svaki je **deseti dan u mjesecu** posvećen Merzu, jer je toga datuma završio svoj zemaljski život. Taj je dan, kaže, „na neki način njegov”, a tada se moli upravo za kanonizaciju. Svoju misao zaključuje s osmijehom: neka dragi Bog „malo požuri gore u Rimu”.

magisterium.assessment: Opisana je molba papi da se blaženi Ivan Merz što prije proglasi svetim, što je u skladu s katoličkim poštovanjem blaženika i legitimnim zauzimanjem za njihovu kanonizaciju. Odluku ipak donosi Crkva nakon propisanog ispitivanja, pa molba ne smije stvarati dojam da je kanonizacija unaprijed sigurna.
concerns: Izraz da se papu „bombardira Merzom” djeluje kao šala; bio bi problematičan samo kad bi poticao neprimjeren pritisak ili sugerirao da je kanonizacija već zajamčena.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko štovanje blaženika usmjereno je na Boga i uključuje zahvalnost za njihovo svjedočanstvo te nasljedovanje njihova kršćanskog života; slike mogu služiti takvoj pobožnosti ako ne vode praznovjerju. Crkva izričito upozorava da se ne smije stvarati dojam kako ispitivanje nečije svetosti jamči buduću kanonizaciju, što je važno razlikovati od same molbe da se postupak dovrši.

magisterium.assessment_en: A petition to the Pope for Blessed Ivan Merz to be declared a saint as soon as possible is described, which is in accordance with Catholic veneration of the blessed and legitimate advocacy for their canonization. The decision, however, is made by the Church after the prescribed examination, so the petition must not create the impression that canonization is certain in advance.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic veneration of the blessed is directed toward God and includes gratitude for their witness and the imitation of their Christian life; images can serve such devotion if they do not lead to superstition. The Church explicitly warns that an impression must not be created that the examination of someone's holiness guarantees future canonization, which is important to distinguish from the petition itself that the process be completed.
concerns_en: The expression that the pope is being “bombarded with Merz” appears to be a joke; it would be problematic only if it encouraged inappropriate pressure or suggested that canonization is already guaranteed.

sections.subtitle_en: Picture presented to the Pope and prayer every tenth of the month
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host recounts the presentation of the picture of Blessed Ivan Merz to the Pope in Rome
sections.content_en:
The host recalls the thousands of signatures that the youth from the Philippines sent to the Holy Father and jokingly says that the new pope is being “bombarded with Merz”. His community contributed to this as well. This year they had, as he says, “the opportunity and honor and grace” to be in Rome **on March 25, on the solemnity of the Annunciation of the Blessed Virgin Mary**, and present the picture of Blessed Ivan Merz to the Pope. Along with the picture, they enclosed a petition that their patron be declared a saint as soon as possible. They also intend to make a copy of the picture for themselves.

P. Nagy emphasizes that all of Merz's devotees are awaiting this and that one should pray for this intention. In the **Bazilika Srca Isusova** in Zagreb, every **tenth day of the month** is dedicated to Merz, because on that date he ended his earthly life. That day is, he says, “in a way his”, and then prayers are offered precisely for canonization. He concludes his thought with a smile: may dear God “hurry up a little up there in Rome”.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak iznosi biografske podatke o predavanju međureligijskog dijaloga, bez tvrdnji koje bi proturječile katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu. Takva je profesorska djelatnost u skladu s crkvenim naglaskom na obrazovanju za međureligijsko razumijevanje i miran suživot.
magisterium.enrichment: U katoličkom shvaćanju međureligijski dijalog ne znači izjednačavanje svih vjera ni odustajanje od naviještanja Krista: on se odvija u istini i ljubavi, uz poštovanje slobode i dostojanstva sugovornika. Crkva ga smatra dijelom svojega evangelizacijskog poslanja, a ne zamjenom za njega; stoga njegovo poučavanje može služiti boljem razumijevanju drugih religija i jasnijem svjedočenju katoličke vjere.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage presents biographical data on the teaching of interreligious dialogue, without claims that would contradict Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. Such professorial activity is in alignment with the Church's emphasis on education for interreligious understanding and peaceful coexistence.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Catholic understanding, interreligious dialogue does not mean equating all faiths nor abandoning the proclamation of Christ: it takes place in truth and love, with respect for the freedom and dignity of the interlocutor. The Church considers it part of its evangelizing mission, not a substitute for it; therefore, teaching it can serve a better understanding of other religions and a clearer witnessing to the Catholic faith.

sections.subtitle: „Program života i rada”: od Orlova i Križara do izlaska iz katakombi
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy citira riječi pape Ivana Pavla II. s beatifikacije u Banjoj Luci
sections.content:
P. Nagy podsjeća na rečenicu koju smatra ključnom. Izgovorio ju je papa, danas svetac, **Ivan Pavao II.** u propovijedi na Merzovoj beatifikaciji u **Banjoj Luci**:

> „Ime Ivana Merza za cijeli jedan naraštaj mladih katolika značilo je program života i rada.”

To, ističe p. Nagy, mora vrijediti i danas. Raduje ga što se među mladima napokon bude inicijative koje Merza prihvaćaju.

Objašnjava i povijesni kontekst papinih riječi. Naraštaj o kojem je papa govorio bio je onaj iz Merzova vremena, kada je on bio na čelu **Orlovske katoličke organizacije**. Nakon nepravde koju je beogradski režim počinio **šestosiječanjskom diktaturom 1929.**, Orlovska je organizacija ukinuta. Njezini su se voditelji odmah reorganizirali i osnovali **Križarsku organizaciju**, po uzoru na tadašnje francuske euharistijske križare. Križari su preuzeli Merzovu baštinu i kao katolička udruga dodatno se razvili sve do 1945., a zatim je, kaže p. Nagy, „poznato što je slijedilo”.

Svoj pregled zaključuje slikom koja povezuje prošlost i sadašnjost: nakon 1945. hrvatski su katolici „išli u katakombe”, a sada iz njih izlaze.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je snažno usklađen s katoličkim naukom: vjerno prenosi poticaj Ivana Pavla II. da Merzov primjer bude program kršćanskog života i djelovanja te ga primjenjuje na današnju mladež. Nema uočljivih teoloških problema; Merz se prikazuje kao uzor koji upućuje na življenje vjere, a ne kao zamjena za Krista.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni kontekst beatifikacijske homilije pojašnjava da Merzova svetost nije prvenstveno značila ljudski uspjeh, nego težnju za sjedinjenjem s Bogom i apostolsko služenje mladima, hranjeno misom, Euharistijom i Božjom riječju. Zato se „program života i rada” najbolje razumije kao poziv na osobni susret s Kristom, vođenje Evanđeljem i svjedočenje riječju i djelima, u skladu s Isusovim pozivom da svjetiljka ne ostane skrivena (Mt 5,15).

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is strongly aligned with Catholic teaching: it faithfully conveys the encouragement of John Paul II for Merz's example to be a program of Christian life and action and applies it to today's youth. There are no noticeable theological issues; Merz is presented as a role model pointing toward living the faith, rather than as a substitute for Christ.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The ecclesial context of the beatification homily clarifies that Merz's holiness did not primarily mean human success, but a striving for union with God and apostolic service to the young, nourished by Mass, the Eucharist, and the Word of God. Therefore, the “program of life and work” is best understood as a call to a personal encounter with Christ, being guided by the Gospel, and witnessing in word and deed, in accordance with Jesus' call that a lamp not remain hidden (Mt 5:15).

sections.subtitle_en: “Program of life and work”: from the Orlovi and Križari to emerging from the catacombs
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy quotes the words of Pope John Paul II from the beatification in Banja Luka
sections.content_en:
Fr. Nagy recalls a sentence he considers key. It was spoken by the Pope, today a saint, **John Paul II**, in the homily at Merz's beatification in **Banja Luka**:

> “The name of Ivan Merz meant a program of life and work for an entire generation of young Catholics.”

This, Fr. Nagy points out, must also apply today. He is glad that initiatives that embrace Merz are finally awakening among young people.

He also explains the historical context of the Pope's words. The generation the Pope spoke of was the one from Merz's time, when he was at the head of the **Orlovska Catholic organization**. After the injustice committed by the Belgrade regime through the **January 6 Dictatorship of 1929**, the Orlovska organization was abolished. Its leaders immediately reorganized and founded the **Križarska organizacija**, modeled after the French Eucharistic crusaders of that time. The Križari took over Merz's heritage and, as a Catholic association, further developed until 1945, and then, Fr. Nagy says, “it is known what followed.”

He concludes his overview with an image connecting the past and the present: after 1945, Croatian Catholics “went into the catacombs,” and now they are emerging from them.

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: klanjanje ili propovijed, knjiga ili krunica
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj postavlja prvo blic pitanje, a p. Božidar Nagy razmišlja o odgovoru
sections.content:
Voditelj napominje da bi se o Merzu i njegovim suradnicima, koji su nakon njegove smrti prenosili njegovu ostavštinu, moglo još dugo govoriti. Izražava nadu da će ta tema doći na red u nekoj drugoj epizodi. Na kraju gostu postavlja nekoliko nenajavljenih **blic pitanja tipa „ili-ili”** i unaprijed upozorava da su neka „malo škakljiva” i provokativna.

**Tišina klanjanja ili propovijed pred punom crkvom?** P. Nagy odbija birati: „I jedno i drugo. Ne možete to odvojiti. To ide zajedno.” Voditelj se slaže da obje stvari imaju svoju vrijednost i moć.

**Knjiga u ruci ili krunica u ruci?** Ovdje gost ima jasan red prioriteta: „U prvom redu krunica u ruci”, a knjiga dolazi nakon nje. Voditelj dodaje da se za krunicu kaže kako je zapravo „malo evanđelje u ruci”, što p. Nagy potvrđuje.

**Duhovna disciplina ili spontanost u vjeri?** Odgovor p. Nagyja proizlazi iz isusovačke duhovnosti. Isusovci, kaže, imaju disciplinirani način molitve, jer treba znati red: kada, što i kako. Spontana molitva dolazi usput. Pritom navodi isusovačko načelo ***contemplativus in actione***, odnosno biti kontemplativan u djelovanju i povezati kontemplaciju, molitvu i svakodnevni rad.

magisterium.assessment: Odgovor odbija suprotstaviti klanjanje i propovijedanje te je u skladu s katoličkim razumijevanjem povezanosti kontemplacije i apostolskog djelovanja. Učenje Crkve potvrđuje da molitva i sjedinjenost s Gospodinom hrane plodnost navještaja, dok apostolski rad ne oslobađa od potrebe za molitvom.
magisterium.enrichment: Klanjanje i navještaj različiti su, ali međusobno povezani oblici kršćanskog života: kontemplacija produbljuje susret s Kristom, a apostolsko djelovanje prenosi drugima ono što je vjernik primio. Crkva također uči da euharistijsko klanjanje ne konkurira misi, nego je s njom povezano jačajući vjernikovu vjeru i pripravu za susret s Kristom.

magisterium.assessment_en: The answer refuses to set Eucharistic adoration and preaching against each other and is in accordance with the Catholic understanding of the connection between contemplation and apostolic activity. The teaching of the Church confirms that prayer and union with the Lord nourish the fruitfulness of proclamation, while apostolic work does not exempt one from the need for prayer.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Eucharistic adoration and proclamation are distinct, but interconnected forms of Christian life: contemplation deepens the encounter with Christ, and apostolic activity transmits to others what the believer has received. The Church also teaches that Eucharistic adoration does not compete with the Mass, but is connected with it, strengthening the believer's faith and preparation for the encounter with Christ.

sections.subtitle_en: Quick-fire questions: Eucharistic adoration or sermon, book or Rosary
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks the first quick-fire question, and p. Božidar Nagy thinks about the answer
sections.content_en:
The host notes that one could speak for a long time about Merz and his collaborators, who passed on his legacy after his death. He expresses hope that this topic will be addressed in another episode. At the end, he asks the guest several unannounced **quick-fire „either-or” questions** and warns in advance that some are „a little tricky” and provocative.

**The silence of Eucharistic adoration or a sermon before a full church?** P. Nagy refuses to choose: „Both. You cannot separate that. It goes together.” The host agrees that both things have their value and power.

**A book in the hand or the Rosary in the hand?** Here the guest has a clear order of priorities: „First of all, the Rosary in the hand”, and the book comes after it. The host adds that the Rosary is said to be actually a „little Gospel in the hand”, which p. Nagy confirms.

**Spiritual discipline or spontaneity in faith?** P. Nagy's answer stems from Jesuit spirituality. Jesuits, he says, have a disciplined way of prayer, because one needs to know the order: when, what, and how. Spontaneous prayer comes along the way. In doing so, he cites the Jesuit principle ***contemplativus in actione***, that is, being contemplative in action and connecting contemplation, prayer, and daily work.

sections.subtitle: Knjiga koja obraća i rad koji ne razdvaja katedru i pastoral
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy govori o knjigama Put k suncu i Zlatna knjiga kao izvorima obraćenja
sections.content:
**Dobra knjiga ili dobar duhovni razgovor?** P. Nagy ipak bira knjigu i objašnjava zašto. Kao primjer navodi **Put k suncu**, zbirku tekstova blaženog Merza. Zna za izričit slučaj: **Mišo Lukenda** iz zajednice **Nanovo rođeni** obratio se upravo na temelju te knjige i cjelokupnog Merza. Sve je to unio u svoju zajednicu, koja po uzoru na blaženika danas ima **formaciju na četiri razine**. Istu su knjigu prihvatili i **Mladi za domovinu u Sesvetama**.

Spominje i **Zlatnu knjigu**, koju je **kardinal Stepinac**, član Merzove Orlovske organizacije, nazvao „suhim zlatom”. Voditelj primjećuje da se ta knjiga ne zove bez razloga tako i zaključuje da dobra knjiga doista može biti dobar razgovor.

**Akademski ili pastoralni rad?** U posljednjem blic pitanju p. Nagy ponovno odgovara iz perspektive isusovačkog reda: to ide zajedno, jer i akademski rad jest, odnosno mora biti, pastoralni rad. Veličinu **svetog Ignacija Lojolskog** vidi upravo u tome što je od samih početaka osnivao brojne kolegije i gimnazije za odgoj i formaciju katoličke mladeži, kakve su postojale i u hrvatskim krajevima.

Zaključuje da je danas posebno važno da kršćani katolici ulaze u akademske krugove i povezuju ono što je povezivao Merz: **vjeru, znanost i kulturu**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: predstavlja duhovno štivo kao mogući poticaj obraćenju i kršćanskoj formaciji, a ne iznosi tvrdnju koja bi proturječila vjeri ili Svetom pismu. Spomenuti primjer obraćenja jest osobno svjedočanstvo, pa sam po sebi ne dokazuje da će ista knjiga na isti način djelovati na svakoga.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje obraćenja obuhvaća promjenu života prema Evanđelju, a njeguje se molitvenim čitanjem Svetoga pisma i sakramentalnim životom; zato duhovna knjiga može biti vrijedan poticaj, ali ne zamjenjuje te temelje. Crkveni nauk također povezuje intelektualnu formaciju s osobnim prianjanjem uz Krista i životom Crkve, pa je formacija na više razina vrijedna kada uključuje takvu cjelovitost.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it presents spiritual reading as a possible impulse for conversion and Christian formation, and does not make a claim that would contradict the faith or Sacred Scripture. The mentioned example of conversion is a personal testimony, so by itself it does not prove that the same book will have the same effect on everyone.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of conversion encompasses a change of life according to the Gospel, and is nurtured by prayerful reading of Sacred Scripture and sacramental life; therefore, a spiritual book can be a valuable impulse, but does not replace these foundations. Church teaching also connects intellectual formation with personal adherence to Christ and the life of the Church, so multi-level formation is valuable when it includes such wholeness.

sections.subtitle_en: A book that converts and work that does not separate the academic chair and pastoral care
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy speaks about the books Put k suncu and Zlatna knjiga as sources of conversion
sections.content_en:
**A good book or a good spiritual conversation?** Fr. Nagy nevertheless chooses the book and explains why. As an example, he cites **Put k suncu**, a collection of texts by Blessed Merz. He knows of a specific case: **Mišo Lukenda** from the community **Nanovo rođeni** converted precisely on the basis of that book and the whole of Merz. He brought all of that into his community, which, modeled after the blessed, today has **formation on four levels**. The same book was also accepted by **Mladi za domovinu in Sesvete**.

He also mentions **Zlatna knjiga**, which **Cardinal Stepinac**, a member of Merz's Eagle organization, called "pure gold". The host notes that this book is not called that without reason and concludes that a good book can indeed be a good conversation.

**Academic or pastoral work?** In the final blitz question, Fr. Nagy again answers from the perspective of the Jesuit order: they go together, because academic work also is, or rather must be, pastoral work. He sees the greatness of **Saint Ignatius of Loyola** precisely in the fact that from the very beginnings he founded numerous colleges and grammar schools for the upbringing and formation of Catholic youth, such as also existed in Croatian regions.

He concludes that today it is especially important for Catholic Christians to enter academic circles and connect what Merz connected: **faith, science, and culture**.

sections.subtitle: „Sve na veću slavu Božju”: zahvala i pogled prema sljedećoj epizodi
sections.screenshot_description: P. Božidar Nagy izgovara isusovačko geslo Omnia ad maiorem Dei gloriam
sections.content:
Voditelj zahvaljuje p. Nagyju na akademskom, pastoralnom i svakom drugom radu kojim se širi glas o blaženom Ivanu Merzu. Spominje i druge svece kojima se gost bavi, a za koje u razgovoru nije ostalo vremena. P. Nagy uzvraća zahvalom za poziv i završava geslom svoga reda: ***Omnia ad maiorem Dei gloriam***, „sve na veću slavu Božju”. Voditelj odgovara: „Amen.”

U odjavi voditelj gledatelje poziva da prate podcast ReDefinicija, da ga lajkaju, dijele i pretplate se, uz šaljivu opasku o „starohrvatskim” izrazima. Napominje i da je sljedeća epizoda već dostupna na profilu na Patreonu.

Na samom kraju slijedi isječak iz najave. Gost sljedeće epizode govori o tome kako se u staroj naciji, u kojoj su mnogi formirani u bivšem sustavu, negativan stav prema Hrvatskoj prenosi na djecu. Takav se stav, kaže, često ne uči izravno, nego ga djeca upijaju od roditelja, baka i djedova kao „vibru” jada i čemera. Zaključuje da, kao što Radu Borić „srce boli” kad vidi mlade kako idu na misu, njega srce boli kad vidi mlade koji su negativni i ponavljaju fraze koje bi teško izgovorili da ih tome netko, makar posredno, nije naučio.

magisterium.assessment: Zahvala za rad na širenju glasa o blaženom Ivanu Merzu i isusovačko geslo „Omnia ad maiorem Dei gloriam” u skladu su s katoličkim naglaskom na zahvalnosti Bogu i usmjeravanju djelovanja prema njegovoj slavi. U prikazanom odlomku nema tvrdnje koja bi proturječila katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusovačka duhovnost razumije „veću slavu Božju” kao nastojanje da se u svim djelima traže Božja volja, čast i služenje, a ne kao težnju za ljudskim priznanjem. Biblijski odjek gesla nalazi se u poticaju da se sve što se čini riječju ili djelom čini u ime Gospodina Isusa, zahvaljujući Bogu Ocu po njemu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The thanksgiving for the work of spreading word about Blessed Ivan Merz and the Jesuit motto "Omnia ad maiorem Dei gloriam" are in accordance with the Catholic emphasis on gratitude to God and directing actions toward his glory. In the presented excerpt, there is no claim that would contradict Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesuit spirituality understands the "greater glory of God" as an endeavor to seek God's will, honor, and service in all deeds, and not as an aspiration for human recognition. A biblical resonance of the motto is found in the exhortation that whatever is done in word or deed be done in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.

sections.subtitle_en: "All for the greater glory of God": thanksgiving and a look toward the next episode
sections.screenshot_description_en: Fr. Božidar Nagy speaks the Jesuit motto Omnia ad maiorem Dei gloriam
sections.content_en:
The host thanks Fr. Nagy for his academic, pastoral, and every other work by which word of Blessed Ivan Merz is spread. He also mentions other saints whom the guest deals with, but for whom no time remained in the conversation. Fr. Nagy reciprocates with thanks for the invitation and concludes with the motto of his order: ***Omnia ad maiorem Dei gloriam***, "all for the greater glory of God." The host responds: "Amen."

In the sign-off, the host invites viewers to follow the podcast ReDefinicija, to like, share, and subscribe to it, with a humorous remark about "old Croatian" terms. He also notes that the next episode is already available on the Patreon profile.

At the very end, an excerpt from the preview follows. The guest of the next episode talks about how in an aging nation, where many were formed in the former system, a negative attitude toward Croatia is passed down to children. Such an attitude, he says, is often not learned directly, but children absorb it from parents, grandmothers, and grandfathers as a "vibe" of misery and bitterness. He concludes that, just as Rada Borić's "heart aches" when she sees young people going to Mass, his heart aches when he sees young people who are negative and repeat phrases they would hardly utter if someone, even indirectly, had not taught them.
